Jefferies University: Insights from Experts
Jefferies University: Insights from Experts
Jefferies University is an executive-level education program that connects independent experts with
institutional investors on matters critical to making informed investment choices. Through this global
program, Jefferies’ clients have the opportunity to meet thought-leaders, innovators and scholars on
a wide range of subjects that may be relevant to building investment portfolios. Topics can be tailored
to suit your needs and delivered in different formats including private or group conference calls, in-
person presentations or via video-conference as well as at our numerous conferences and summits
held around the world.
Jefferies University: Exponential Series
Jefferies University courses go beyond investment matters. Our Exponential Series also delves into
issues that can impact investors on a personal level. Join us for sessions that may unlock meaningful
insights relating to your health and well-being, personal development, family dynamics, professional
growth and significant cultural issues.
Restricted to Jefferies’ clients, the program will continuously adapt to meet your needs and help
identify the latest industry trends, investment ideas and macro developments that matter to you most.
Important Disclosure
Any views or opinions expressed by the third-party experts are solely those of the speaker, not
Jefferies, and this does not represent an endorsement by Jefferies of the views or opinions
expressed.

For more information, suggestions and feedback, please contact JefferiesUniversity@Jefferies.com.

Aparajit Bhandarkar
Aparajit leads the Alternative Investments Practice at Varanium. He comes with 24+ years
of experience in Investment Banking, Investor Relations, and startup investments. Served as
CEO of Dice Fintech Ace, a Fintech Venture Fund. Prior to that, he was Head of Strategy at Jio
Payments Bank. He also held several senior leadership positions at Yes Bank, where he was
among the first 50 employees, including President – Merchant Banking and Head of Investor        .

Relations, and successfully led two QIPs. He holds an MBA from NYU (Stern) and is CFA
Charterholder (USA), and a CA.

Aman Jain
Aman Jain has over 7 years of experience across venture investments, strategy, research,
and valuations. At Varanium, he is part of the venture capital and venture debt investment
team. Prior to joining the firm, he worked at Evalueserve as a Research Analyst covering U.S.
consumer discretionary and automotive sectors. Aman is a CA and a CFA (USA), and he also
holds a Bachelor’s degree in Financial Markets.

Enabler #1: Strong India-Stack and incentives aided strong growth
In the past five years, India has benefited from the confluence of a strong India-Stack (for payments,
lending, identification & documentation, etc.), strong fintech app interface, attractive incentive
structure, a tech-adaptive population, and low-cost access to data & mobile technology. These have
aided strong growth across all segments of fintech use-cases in India. Over FY20-25, India has seen
online payments rise at 48% CAGR, P2P part rose at 36%, and the share of cash transactions has
declined from 81% to 55%, market for digital insurance has grown at 28% Cagr, digital lending at
18% and equity/ derivative trading using digital-first trading platforms has grown at 64%.

1.    Aadhaar: This is a unique 12-digit identification number assigned to residents of India based on their biometric and demographic data. It
      serves as a foundation for various digital services, including authentication and eKYC (Know Your Customer) processes.
2.    Electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC): This is a paperless process that uses Aadhaar-based authentication to verify the identity of
      individuals when accessing services or conducting transactions.
3.    Digital Lockers: This allows individuals to securely store and share their documents and certificates electronically. This service reduces the
      need for physical documents and streamlines administrative processes.
4.    eSign: This is a digital signature service that allows individuals to electronically sign documents, contracts, and agreements. It eliminates
      the need for physical signatures and offers a secure and legally valid alternative.
5.    Digital Consent: This mechanism enables individuals to grant permission to share their personal data with specific entities for specific
      purposes. This enhances data privacy and control.
6.    Digital Authentication: This leverages Aadhaar-based authentication to verify the identity of individuals accessing digital services securely
      and conveniently.

Payments

1.    Unified Payment Interface (UPI): This is a real-time payment system that facilitates instant fund transfers between bank accounts using
      mobile phones. It simplifies peer-to-peer transactions and enables cashless payments.
2.    Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT): This is a system that facilitates the direct transfer of subsidies and benefits from the government to
      beneficiaries’ bank accounts. It reduces leakages and ensures efficient delivery of benefits.
3.    Aadhaar-Enabled Payment System (AePS): AePS enables individuals to perform basic banking transactions like cash withdrawals and
      balance inquiries using Aadhaar authentication, even without a bank account. The DBT mission was moved to the Cabinet Secretariat for
      greater impetus, and an electronic payment framework was established.
4.    Jan Dhan Accounts: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) (2014) aimed at financial inclusion provided bank accounts to all Indians.

Commerce, Lending, Insurance

1.    ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce): This is an initiative to democratize e-commerce, similar to UPI for payments, creating open
      rails for digital commerce.
2.    OCEN (Open Credit Enablement Network): This is an open, standardized platform that connects borrowers (especially MSMEs) with various
      lenders via APIs, democratizing access to quick, small, and affordable loans by streamlining data sharing and loan processes.
3.    Loan Service Provider (LSP): These are digital platforms that act as intermediaries to facilitate the entire lending process, connecting
      borrowers with lenders on the OCEN.
4.    Account Aggregator (AA): This is a consent-based data-sharing layer that lets users securely share their financial data (bank, mutual funds,
      insurance, GST/tax) with financial service providers (lenders, fintechs) via neutral, data-blind intermediaries called AAs.
5.    Bima Sugam: This is a digital marketplace proposed by the IRDAI to centralise and simplify India's insurance processes.
6.    Health and Governance: Platforms like Co-WIN (vaccination management), Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (digital health), and
      Government e-Marketplace (GeM).

Enabler #2: Favourable demographics and affordable data helped
India has benefited from a younger and aspiring population cohort, with a median age of 29 years
compared to 40 years in China and higher in developed countries too. This along with access
to smartphones and affordable cost of data aided penetration of digital commerce. Additionally,
the government's intervention, particularly making UPI a zero-MDR platform during events like
demonetisation & Covid, further accelerated the shift toward digital payments.

Enabler #3: AI across verticals
Companies across verticals are investing in building capabilities on AI & ML in terms of payments, underwriting, loan-processing & collections,
operational efficiencies, call center automation, and fraud prevention among others. One of the key areas in which AI and language models can

Page 12

                                                                                                           Expert Studies | India | Financials

help companies is to organize scattered data (over physical documents, conversations and external sources) into analytical models to drive
revenues, and reduce leakages. We have summarized some of the use cases across verticals below:

Payments:

•     Agentic payments & conversational commerce: GenAI models, when integrated with UPI, can enable end-to-end transactions within the
      chat interfaces.
•     Fraud prevention: Deployment of behavioural biometrics, device intelligence, and network graph models to counter rising fraud sophistication
      (synthetic IDs, deepfake KYC, merchant collusion).
•     Merchant intelligence & retention analytics: This strengthens merchant stickiness by predicting churn, optimising pricing and incentives,
      and providing self-serve business insights in user-friendly language.
•     Self-healing & autonomous operations: AI monitors POS devices, gateways, and networks to detect and fix failures automatically, supporting
      c.100% uptime at scale.

LendTech:

•     Automated underwriting and decision-making: This helps to reduce manual intervention in loan approvals, improve turnaround time and
      lower underwriting costs, esp. for small-ticket loans.
•     Alternative data-based credit scoring: Lenders use transaction-level data, platform payouts, and other non-bureau signals to assess NTC
      borrowers (borrowers with less credit history).
•     Sector-specific or vertical-specific risk models: Industry-specific feature engineering helps better capture business cycle and operating
      metrics, which can support more differentiated pricing and risk selection.
•     End-to-end digital loan processing, collections and portfolio monitoring: Automated workflows from origination to disbursal, contributing
      to lower opex and improved scalability. Predictive models used to prioritise collection efforts & identify early signs of stress.

WealthTech:

•     Portfolio Intelligence: AI aims to deliver dynamic, context-aware systems that continuously interpret portfolio data, market events, and
      investor behaviour, positioning platforms as an intelligent decision-support layer. Trading companies use LLMs for quality assurance and
      ML-based nudges to prevent reckless trading.
•     Conversational interfaces for investing: LLMs (Large Language Models) & RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) architectures turn
      portfolios into queriable datasets (e.g., “What changed after the Budget?”). Companies use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to deliver portfolio
      intelligence layer that securely connects LLMs to user accounts.
•     Product curation: In thematic and basket-based investing, ML models are automating stock selection, rebalancing, and signal generation.
      Companies use these to deliver predictive baskets that target specific quantitative outcomes (e.g., 3% returns in 30 days), moving beyond
      static thematic baskets to automated stock selection, portfolio construction, and rebalancing driven by AI signals.

InsurTech:

•     Claims settlement: AI enables faster checks of documentation, prescription matching, and fraud detection. Faster turnaround directly
      improves NPS (Net Promoter Score), retention, and renewal rates. AI is shifting claims from a cost centre to a customer acquisition lever.
•     Automation of the loss assessment layer: Computer Vision and ML models are replacing manual surveyors in motor and health insurance,
      enabling straight-through processing (STP) for low-severity claims and materially reducing turnaround times. Companies are leveraging
      technology to enable zero-touch claims, eliminate physical surveyors for minor claims and enable STP.
•     Fraud prevention: Moving fraud detection from post-claim audits to pre-issuance and early-claim screening, using behavioral signals,
      document forensics, and anomaly detection to protect loss ratios. Companies have indicated that ML-based fraud models flag 10–15% of
      policies as high-risk early in the lifecycle.
•     Voice & language models: Insurers and aggregators are deploying Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) and Natural Language Processing
      (NLP) models trained on Indian languages to monitor sales calls, reduce mis-selling, and improve compliance with regulations.

Source: Varanium, Jefferies
Central Currency (CBDC) is a digital form of a country's fiat currency issued and regulated by its central bank. CBDCs are designed to be similar
to cryptocurrencies, but they may not require blockchain technology or consensus mechanisms. CBDCs can be developed in a number of ways,
including centralized and decentralized approaches. In a centralized approach, the central bank manages the ledgers that record transactions
and also provides user-facing services. In a decentralized approach, the central bank sets rules and requirements for CBDC transactions, which
are then recorded by users or financial intermediaries. Key use cases include: 1) Automated Tax Deduction / Collection at Source using CBDC,
2) DBT, 3) Trade Finance, 4) Wealth Management and 5) Cross Border Payment.

Digital Rupee or e₹, is India's Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). It is the digital form of India's physical currency, the Rupee (₹). e₹ is issued by
the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in digital form and e₹ is at par with the physical currency, offering features similar to physical cash like convenience
of use, guarantee of RBI, finality of settlement, etc. e₹ is stored in the user's digital wallet and can be used to receive / send money, and / or make
payment for transactions, just like any physical ₹ note. As the money is held in a wallet and is equivalent to cash, customers don't earn interest
income on it. The offline architecture uses NFC communication on merchant POS terminals and Bluetooth to facilitate transactions in areas with
limited or zero internet connectivity.

e₹ is a digital form of ₹ whereas UPI is a means of payment. In addition to being used for payments, e₹ also serves as a ‘store of value’, i.e., e₹
can be withdrawn from one’s bank account and kept separately in the e₹ wallet. In the case of P2P and P2M payments made at any CBDC QR,
the transactions happen between two e₹ wallets, and are settled instantaneously without passing through user’s bank accounts. For P2P and
P2M payments, the functionality to scan a UPI QR code from an e₹ app has also been enabled. In such cases, the settlement will be based on
the UPI settlement timelines.

The use of e₹ is currently being piloted through some studies in the country. The pilot is being tried in the Retail (public) and Wholesale (bank and
other institutions) segments. Currently, 19 banks are offering CBDC wallets for retail segment and 16 for wholesale segment.

Tokenisation                                                                                              ALT ID (Nov-23) replaces PAN for
                                                                                                          downstream processing, cutting sensitive
Tokenization replaces sensitive card PAN (the 16-digit card number) with a non-sensitive token
                                                                                                          card-data exposure
that can be safely stored and used for transactions, while the original PAN remains protected with
authorised card networks/issuers.

In India, RBI’s Card-on-File (CoF) storage restriction took effect on 1st Oct 2022, meaning entities in
the payment chain should not store actual card data. For guest checkout (manual card entry each
time), the ecosystem introduced ALT ID (alternate identifier instead of PAN) to support downstream
needs like capture/refund/reconciliation without propagating PAN which was effective from 1st
Nov 2023. From a customer lens, this is a major security uplift as it materially reduces sensitive card
data exposure, supports data minimisation, lowers breach impact, and improves audit readiness
by shrinking PCI scope and strengthening controls, while still enabling saved cards, recurring
payments, and one-click checkout.

The trade-off is higher complexity and cost due to changes across checkout, retries, refunds/
chargebacks, reconciliation and reporting, plus ongoing testing/monitoring and dependency
on token/ALT-ID rails and uptime. While tokenization exists globally, India’s combination of
ecosystem-wide CoF purge plus an ALT ID model designed for guest checkout at national scale is
unusually comprehensive for a large market and sets a high bar for card-security posture.

As growth normalizes, we believe that companies will need to accelerate the monetization of their
customer base through a combination of revenue-linked services and operating efficiencies. The
good news over the past few years is that companies have withdrawn discounts & incentives to

tightening of data privacy laws. We believe that companies that struggle to monetise their customer
base may be forced to consolidate or merge into larger players, especially as ability to raise capital
is likely to get tougher. We have discussed the revenue and profit generation trends in the industry

Tailwinds and headwinds to monetization                                                                                               Payment segment is likely to see a ramp-up
There are some tailwinds and headwinds to monetization opportunities for fintechs, evident in                                         of credit on UPI, allowing platforms to offer
select segments. In the Payment segment, the tailwind is likely to emerge from ramp-up of credit                                      credit
on UPI, which will allow platforms offering UPI payments to offer credit. Currently, this is open only
to credit lines from banks, but in our opinion, it may also open to credit from NBFCs, which we see
as a larger opportunity. In this segment, the headwind can be from recent restrictions from the RBI
on payment of rent and education fees using credit cards on fintech platforms. Also, the regulator
has discontinued PIDF incentive scheme that was providing cash incentives to platforms to expand
presence in smaller towns & cities.

These were key driver of revenues for some of the larger platforms, and they are engaging with
the regulator on the approach for this segment in the future. From our coverage, Paytm is well-
placed to benefit from expansion in credit opportunity on UPI rails and ability to scale-up BNPL-
like lending business within comfort of the regulator. We also see negligible impact on revenues
from restrictions on rent and education services as well as real-money-gaming (RMG) as they made
small contribution to revenues & profits.

which primarily came for either stock-trading or mutual funds (direct). The opportunity to cross                                      incremental revenue in WealthTech
sell LAS, MTF, personal loans products is likely to drive revenue opportunity for players in this
segment. On the flip side, this segment may also be at risk if SEBI tightens norms on index options
derivatives that can impact revenues from transactions as well as float positions that clients carry
with wealthtechs. From our coverage, Groww is a dominant player in this segment, and we see it

commissions.

Regulatory action is high, but should normalise
Over the past few years, the RBI and the Government have tightened regulations relevant to fintechs.
These include waiver of MDR on UPI, restrictions on aspects such as credit card products from
fintechs, BNPL, P2P lending, use of credit cards to pay rent/ education. Ban on real money gaming
affected payments platforms and tightening of norms on cash business affected wealth platforms.
The proposed tightening of regulations around data privacy and usage of customer data can also
impact the extent of monetization among platforms. While some of these restrictions will impact
profit pools in FY26-27, industry is looking at ways to minimise impact and enhance profit pools.
At the same time, we also note that in Oct-23, RBI had approved the merger of North East Small
Finance Bank with Slice to be setup as Slice North East Small Finance Bank.

Key restrictions and regulations:                                                                                                               In Jun-23, RBI tightened FLDG norms,
Credit cards and Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL): Non-banking BNPL providers are restricted from                                                       constraining growth in short-term and small-
loading credit lines onto Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs), such as digital wallets or prepaid                                                ticket loans
cards. This forced many providers to change their business models. The Digital Lending Directions
mandate transparent disclosure of the Annual Percentage Rate (APR), loan tenure, fees, and the
name of the regulated entity (RE) providing the loan for all digital lending activities, which includes
many BNPL services. In Sept-22, the RBI cautioned against the rapid growth of short-tenure and
small-value loans, including BNPL products. Subsequently, in Jun-23, it tightened norms on First
Loss Default Guarantee (FLDG) arrangements, further constraining growth in the segment.

Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Lending: In 2024, RBI introduced new measures for P2P lending platforms                                                      In 2024, RBI barred P2P platforms from
that impacted growth to streamline the businesses. These restricted P2P platforms from offering                                                 offering credit guarantees, assured returns,
credit-risk guarantees, assured returns or investment marketing, capped lending limit to Rs5m                                                   or marketing investments
with certification requirement when loan crosses Rs1m, escrow account mandate with T+1

settlement, manual and individual borrower selection, restriction on cross-selling of financial

Digital Lending regulations: In May 2025, the RBI issued Digital Lending Directions to address          In May-25, RBI rose compliance &
consumer protection risks in India’s digital lending sector. Its key provisions were (1) Ban on Sales   accountability for REs, while raising opex &
Role for Lending Service Providers (LSPs): LSPs cannot act as salesmen or promote specific              tightening marketing norms for LSPs
lenders and multi-lender platforms must display unbiased loan offers matching borrower requests,
(2) Transparency & Consumer Protection: No dark patterns or deceptive UI designs and mandatory
disclosure of Name of lender, Loan features (tenor, APR, monthly repayment, penal charges),
prominent link to Key Fact Statement (KFS) and charges not disclosed in KFS cannot be levied later,
(3) Increased accountability: REs remain fully liable for acts of LSPs, mandatory contracts defining
roles and obligations and REs must conduct due diligence and periodic reviews of LSPs, and (4)
Data Privacy & Localization: Strict data minimization and explicit consent rules, DLAs cannot
access sensitive phone data (contacts, media), borrowers can withdraw consent and request data
deletion and all borrower data must be stored on Indian servers; foreign data must be deleted
within 24 hours. The impact: (1) For REs: Increased compliance burden and accountability, (2) For
LSPs: Higher operational costs, restrictions on marketing, (3) For Consumers: Greater transparency,
reduced mis-selling, improved data privacy.

Credit cards for Rent, Education Fees: The practice of using credit lines to load non-bank PPIs has     Discontinuation of the PIDF scheme from
been banned. In Nov-25, RBI's updated Payment Aggregator (PA) guidelines mandate that fintech           Jan-26 may weigh on earnings of Payment
platforms can only process payments for merchants with whom they have a direct contractual              companies
agreement and complete Know Your Customer (KYC) compliance, which will impact use of credit
cards in segments like rent and education fees.

PIDF scheme discontinued. The Payments Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) was
introduced by the RBI to accelerate the adoption of digital payments, especially in underpenetrated
regions. The scheme focused on supporting the deployment of Point of Sale machines, QR code
based payment systems, and Soundbox and Aadhaar enabled payment devices. The corpus of this
scheme was set at Rs10bn, but the scheme has been discontinued from Jan 2026 onwards and
will impact earnings of companies like Paytm and other QR/ sound-box based payments platforms.

Data Privacy: India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023, with its 2025 rules,
can impact the fintech industry as it mandates explicit consent, data minimization, stronger
security, and user rights (like deletion). This may require tech overhauls for consent management,
encryption, and breach reporting.

Payments landscape                                                                                                                                                   We profile 22 payment cos with aggregate
                                                                                                                                                                     revenues of c.Rs512bn & a combined mkt
India's payment segment is a diversified one, where companies have chosen to focus on B2C,
                                                                                                                                                                     valuation of ~US$55bn
B2B, online, offline payments, specific use cases for customers like gift cards, credit cards and/
or operate though the Payments Bank license. The payments segment has benefitted from strong
growth in TPV that has grown at 48% Cagr over FY20-25 aided by surge in UPI based payments
along with growth in credit cards that have taken market share from debit card and wallet based
payments. However, the low take rates (especially on UPI), higher competition and fixed costs have
limited profitability in this segment.

Over FY25-30, growth in payment volumes is likely to be moderate at 16% CAGR and this may reflect
in slower revenue growth trends also. Our conversation with companies indicates that they plan to
control Opex growth to improve profitability. However, some companies in this segment may face
pressure on profitability due to recent RBI's mandate on restricting real-money gaming, payment
of rent and education services through credit cards. This has also led to realignment of valuation
of companies in this segment.

We profile 19 payment companies in this segment with aggregate revenues of c.Rs512bn and
market valuation (based on market cap and last deal) of ~US$55bn. Among these listed players,
One97 Communications (Paytm) is the leader and has leveraged its payments and merchant
network to cross-sell loan products and diversifying into wealth/ broking, credit on UPI/ BNPL and
other products. Pine Labs is a leader in POS/ DCP payments, affordability solutions and gift cards
in India. Mobikwik and Zaggle were recently listed in payments and corporate expending / gift card
segment. Among Payments Banks (PB), Fino PB recently got in-principle approval to transition into
small-finance-bank and other players are Jio PB, Airtel PB and India Post PB. Companies like CRED,
Juspay, Cashfree among others have built larger market share and revenue pools.

Paytm (One 97 Communications Limited)                                                                                                     Paytm operates a Payments platform and
                                                                                                                                          distributes financial products with revenue
Paytm was founded in 2000 by Vijay Shekhar Sharma (CEO). It operates a UPI platform and
                                                                                                                                          scale of Rs69bn in FY25
distributes financial products, including merchant working capital and personal loans, while not
retaining lending risk on its balance sheet. Operations are primarily focused in India, with increasing
penetration across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.

Paytm’s revenue is driven by a) payment processing commissions, b) merchant subscription fees,
and c) distribution fees from financial services products. As of Mar-26, the platform reported 15mn
paying subscription merchants and a Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) of Rs24tn.

FY25 financial performance saw a contraction in topline alongside improved loss metrics due to
restrictions imposed by the RBI, but it has seen improvement in FY26 on revenues as well as
operating efficiency. Revenue stood at Rs69bn in FY25, declining 31% YoY from Rs100bn in FY24.
Net loss narrowed to Rs7bn in FY25 from Rs14bn in the prior year. Over FY22-25, revenue increased
at a CAGR of 11.5%, while adj EBITDA losses reduced from Rs15bn in FY22 to Rs7bn in FY25,
progressing toward operating breakeven through cost rationalisation and business realignment.

Recent strategic actions include the sale of the entertainment ticketing business to Zomato
for Rs20bn in August 2025, supporting balance sheet strengthening and sharper focus on core
payments and financial services. The company also secured a Payment Aggregator license from
the RBI in late 2025, reinforcing regulatory compliance and enabling broader merchant onboarding.

Paytm's current market cap is Rs771bn ($8.3bn). It raised Rs183bn via an IPO in Nov-21. As of
Dec-25, Vijay Shekhar Sharma holds a 10% stake and institutional investors include SAIF Partners
(13%), Resilient Asset Management (10%), and Antfin (6%).

prepaid and gift card solutions. While India remains its core market with over 1.9m DCP devices at
1mn active merchants and annual GTV exceeding Rs11tn as on FY25, international operations in
the UAE, Malaysia, and Singapore contribute c.15% of revenue as on June 2025.

In FY25, revenue rose to Rs23bn, up 28.5% YoY, while Adjusted EBITDA reached Rs3.6bn with a
15.7% margin. Net Loss narrowed to Rs1.5bn, improving from Rs3.4bn in FY24. Revenue grew at
a 19% CAGR over FY23-25, while Adjusted EBITDA expanded to Rs3.6bn (vs Rs0.6bn in FY23),
reflecting margin gains from operating leverage despite finance costs impacting net earnings in
FY24. The company completed its public listing in Nov 2025, introduced Credit on UPI, and achieved
net profitability in FY26, supported by cost rationalization.

The company's current market cap stood at Rs180bn ($2bn) close to its Nov 2025 listing valuation.
Shareholding is led by Peak XV Partners (17%), followed by Temasek (6%) and PayPal (5%).

Avenues AI Limited (formerly known as Infibeam Avenues)                                               Avenues     AI    operates     a    payments
                                                                                                      infrastructure platform, with FY26 revenue of
Avenues AI Limited was founded by Vishal Mehta and Vishwas Patel and is headquartered in
                                                                                                      Rs81bn
Gandhinagar, India. Vishal Mehta serves as Chairman, MD, and CEO, while Vishwas Patel is the Joint
Managing Director. The company operates a payments infrastructure platform anchored by its core
payment gateway brand, CCAvenue, offering online payment aggregation, settlement services, and
merchant value-added solutions. Revenue is driven by transaction processing volumes and take
rates, with volumes diversified across India and international markets such as the UAE and Saudi
Arabia, where take rates are higher.

A key recent development is the RBI final authorization in Nov-25, permitting Avenues AI to operate
as a Payment Aggregator Physical, enabling offline payment products including SoundBox and
TapPay. It also completed the slump sale of its platform business to subsidiary Rediff.com Limited
in Aug2025 for Rs8bn.

Total payment value grew by 55% YoY to Rs5,038bn in FY26, & active merchants exceeded 10mn.
Revenue doubled YoY to Rs81bn in FY26. Adjusted Ebitda (ex-ESOPs) grew 8% YoY to Rs3.6bn in
FY26 (vs Rs3.3bn, FY24), while adj Ebitda margins halved to 4% in FY26 (vs 8%, FY25). Profit rose
to Rs3bn in FY26 compared to Rs2.4bn in FY25, 25% YoY increase, aided by higher other income.
Revenue recorded a 58% Cagr over FY22-26, & adj Ebitda grew at a 24% Cagr over the same period.
Adj Ebitda margins declined from 12% in FY22 to 4% in FY26.

Company's market cap is Rs60bn (US$0.65bn). As of Sep-25, promoter shareholding stands at
27%, with Vishal Mehta holding 9%, Vishwas Patel holding 10%, and Infinium Motors holding 8%.
Institutional investors include Vanguard and BlackRock.

MobiKwik (One Mobikwik Systems Limited)                                                                  MobiKwik operates across Payments (65%
                                                                                                         of revenues) & lending services (35%), with
MobiKwik, founded in 2009 by Bipin Preet Singh (CEO) & Upasana Taku and headquartered in
                                                                                                         FY26 revenues of Rs11bn
Gurugram, operates as a digital financial services platform. The company operates a consumer
payments-led platform with lending & financial services as additional offerings. The business model
spans Wallet, UPI (including Pocket UPI), BBPS, merchant acquiring, payment gateway through
Zaakpay, and unsecured lending including BNPL and merchant loans.

In FY26, MobiKwik received multiple regulatory licenses, including a) NBFC license, b) Offline
Payment Aggregator license, & c) Online Payment Aggregator license. A broking licence (BSE &
SEBI approval received) is under development with a small team, targeted for launch by FY27,
with limited near-term revenue contribution but longer-term optionality. MobiKwik is scaling up
merchant payments as a key growth vertical, while continuing its existing lending distribution (LSP)
business and introducing a captive NBFC as an additional, not replacement, lending vehicle. Initially,
only a small share of loans will be routed through the NBFC, but management expects it to drive
better unit economics, enable faster product experimentation, & provide greater flexibility along with
access to a wider set of funding partnerships, including co-lending with banks to scale lending more
efficiently over time. It has made a Rs100mn capital infusion into its NBFC subsidiary to enable
own-book lending.

In Payments, Mobikwik remains the leader in wallets with c.18-20% market share vs 3-5% for peers,        MobiKwik expects merchant payments to
supported by strong product features and UPI integration. UPI volumes have improved on the               become a meaningful revenue contributor by
consumer side (slightly improved UPI market share in FY26), while BBPS is already among the top          FY28
3-4 players. Its working capital usage is limited to payment settlement cycles (1-3 days), funded via
bank lines at c.10-10.5% cost, translating to c.Rs70mn per quarter. Management expects to grow
the Payments GMV to grow at 50-60% Cagr over FY26-28.

MobiKwik's lending book constitutes of c.32% super prime, 46% prime, & 22% near prime
customers, all with bureau scores above 700 (54% above 750). The product mix is shifting away
from BNPL towards longer-tenure EMI-based PLs with typical tenures of 12-18 months. Its FY26
loan disbursements stood at c.Rs32bn, with management guiding for a 30-40% Cagr over FY26-28
in lending disbursements going ahead, while maintaining underwriting discipline (focus on prime
& super prime) to preserve asset quality.

Management expects merchant payments to become a meaningful revenue contributor by FY28,
up from a current run-rate of Rs200-300mn, with scale-up driven by 5-6x growth in device
deployments & 10x revenue expansion over three years. The focus remains on profitable segments
generating device rentals and MDR, with soundboxes earning Rs90-100/month per device and EDC
terminals delivering higher economics via rental plus MDR, supporting strong operating leverage
& merchant monetisation.

On profitability & margins, management remains comfortable sustaining current margins, with an
overall contribution margin target of 46-48% over the next two years (vs c.38-40% currently). With
operating leverage expected to kick in, Ebitda margins are guided to reach at least c.10% over the
medium term.

As of FY26, the platform serves over 189mn registered users and 4.8mn merchants, processing a
Payments GMV of Rs1,821bn. In FY26, revenue fell to Rs11bn (-4% YoY), while net losses narrowed
to Rs621mn & adj. EBITDA margin stood at -3%. Revenue Cagr over FY22-26 was c.21% and losses
at PAT level shrunk from Rs1,282mn in FY22 to losses amounting to Rs621mn in FY26 with better
cost discipline & improving operating efficiency.

The company has a market cap of c.Rs16bn (US$0.2bn). Shareholding comprises promoters Bipin
Preet Singh and Upasana Taku (25%), Bajaj Finance Limited (10%), and Peak XV Partners (10%).

CRED (Dreamplug Technologies Private Limited)                                                                                              Cred targets affluent “India 1” users,
                                                                                                                                           with FY25 revenue of Rs24bn split
Cred was founded in 2018 by Kunal Shah and is headquartered in Bengaluru. It is a fintech
platform focused on affluent “India 1” consumers with credit scores above 750, built around a gated
community experience. The company initially offered reward-led credit card bill payments and

                                                                                                                               July 14, 2026

has since expanded into a broader financial ecosystem comprising lending, vehicle management           across payments (40%), lending (40%), and
via CRED Garage, and wealth management capabilities supported by the acquisitions of Kuvera,           insurance (15%)
Spenny, and CreditVidya. In Jun-26, Kunal Shah stepped down as CEO, however he will continue
to hold shares in Cred. Miten Sampat, who has led strategy & finance at Cred since 2020, was
appointed as the interim CEO.

Revenues arise from payments incl. rent and education fees (40% of FY25 revenue), lending (40%),
insurance (15%), marketing, and other services. Recently, RBI tightened norms on payment of
rent and education fees using credit cards on fintech platforms - so clarity on this will be key
for payments platforms. Focus will be on increasing cross-sells, ramping-up wealth platform and
aligning on regulations regarding payment of rent & education fees.

Two primary user needs drive activity: reward optimisation and short-term credit. Credit card users
load PPI wallets for peer payments; about 5% of credit card spends go towards loading PPIs. User
engagement improved to around 20 monthly sessions per user, up from 18 in the previous year.
Earlier users used Cred only for credit-card bill payments, but today, 60% use at least two products
out of the eight available. Signing up the receiver directly remains preferred for control. About
45% engage with online commerce. Offline engagement continues. Around 35% are active on Cred
Garage and the platform is among the largest distributors of motor insurance. About 33% track
credit scores and 33% manage utility bills.

Monthly active users (MAU) are 16mn who open the app at least once to check bills. About
13.5mn are monthly transacting (MTU) users and these users form the monetised base. Total
Payment Value (TPV) increased 55% YoY to Rs69bn, while CRED Pay and P2P UPI transactions
recorded 254% YoY growth, with the platform accounting for nearly 1% of India’s total UPI volumes.
Payments contribute about 40% of revenue, lending contributes 40%, insurance 15% and other
streams 5%. Rent sits inside the payments segment and accounts for Rs6bn of revenue. Gross
revenue is about Rs27bn, with net revenue at 67% or about Rs18bn.

Cred has originated Rs800bn in personal loans over its lifetime and collected Rs570bn, with
Rs230bn as the open book. The business has gone through cycles, including Covid and corrections
within unsecured lending. In FY25, Gross revenue was c.Rs27bn (17-18% YoY), with net revenue
at 67% or about Rs18bn. Gross margins improved 58% YoY due to pricing power across certain
products and stronger unit economics. For every Rs100 in gross revenue, the cost of service is
Rs30-35, leading to a 67% gross margin. The platform monetises about 30% of monthly transacting
users. Contirbution margin 1 (CM1) moved from 67% to 40-45% in FY25. Cash burn has reduced
to a lower level in FY25, with quarterly cash burn fallen about 70% to c.US$2mn. In FY24, company
reported Adjusted Ebitda loss of Rs10bn and net loss of Rs16bn.

In FY25, we understand that management expects an improvement in both contribution and gross
margins, albeit muted headline growth. Over the next two to three years, tightening of norms on rent
& education payments is likely have high impact on Cred. Ex of that, it aims for 25-30% growth. The
platform holds a 9-10% share of the personal-loan market and aims to reach 15-20% by increasing
ticket sizes, which have grown from Rs360k to Rs430k. The card business may form 5-6% of
revenue by the third year as a separate line. Insurance aims to move from 1.2mn to 4-5mn policies.
Mutual fund or international investing offerings may launch through a separate app, leading to three
apps: a) Cred, b) Kuber and c) new wealth-related product.

CRED was valued at c.Rs420bn ($4.5bn) following Meta's US$900mn investment for a 20% stake
in Jun-26. Previously, the company was valued at c.Rs300bn. Investment funds dominate the cap
table with a 74% ownership, led by Peak XV Partners at 10% and GIC at 6%. Kunal Shah holds a 12%
stake, while the employee stock option pool accounts for 11%.

operates a Revenue Growth Management platform offering modules for billing, retention, revenue
recognition, and receivables, generating revenue through subscription fees and overage charges
on billing volume from a global client base of B2B SaaS and ecommerce merchants.

above 150%.

Ebitda (pre-ESOP) at Rs636mn was up 2% YoY with margins steady at 16%. PAT was Rs403mn,
rising 10% YoY (vs Rs368mn in FY23). Revenue grew at a Cagr of 34%, while adj EBITDA grew at
38% Cagr over FY21-25 with margins expanding by 2pp over the same period.

The company was last valued at Rs262bn ($3.5bn) during a $250mn Series H round in Feb 2022
led by Tiger Global and Peak XV Partners. Key investors include Tiger Global, Insight Partners, Peak
XV Partners, and Sapphire Ventures, with founders retaining operational control.

BharatPe (Resilient Innovations Private Limited)                                                                                         BharatPe is a merchant-centric Payments
                                                                                                                                         (60% revenue) & Lending platform, with FY25
BharatPe is an India-focused financial technology platform founded by Ashneer Grover, Shashvat
                                                                                                                                         revenue of Rs17bn
Nakrani, and Bhavik Koladiya. Nalin Negi serves as the CEO. The company operates a merchant-
centric payments and lending platform with a pan-India footprint. BharatPe’s revenue model is
diversified across Financial Services and Payments. Financial Services has been the primary
contributor, accounting for c.60% of total revenue, while Payments contributed the remaining over
the same period.

The registered merchant base expanded from 13mn in FY24 to 17mn in FY25, reflecting steady
onboarding momentum. Annualized TPV increased from Rs2.2tn in FY24 to Rs2.6tn in FY25, while
Soundbox device deployments rose from 3.2mn to over 3.5mn during the same period.

In FY25, company reported revenues of Rs17bn, up 17% YoY, and a net loss of Rs883m vs.
Rs5bn in FY24. It also booked one-time gain of Rs726bn on settlement case. In FY24, revenues
from operation were at Rs14bn that included Rs8.5bn from financial services. Over FY22-24, total
revenue increased at a CAGR of 77%. Profitability improved materially during this phase. Adjusted
EBITDA posted a loss of Rs1,556mn in FY24, while FY25 marked a turnaround with Adjusted
EBITDA of Rs1,958mn. The company's losses have reduced to Rs883mn (vs 4,900mn, FY24). The
improvement was supported by reduced marketing expenses and a higher contribution from the
Financial Services segment.

BharatPe plans to sell part of its 49% stake in Unity Small Finance Bank (SFB), partly to comply RBI
norms that cap shareholding in bank to 10% by 2029. As per media report (Business Standard 3
Jan 2025) the stake may be valued at US$800m.

The latest disclosed valuation for BharatPe is Rs200bn ($2.7bn), following its Series E funding round
in August 2021. The shareholding structure is led by Peak XV Partners, with Coatue Management
and Ribbit Capital among other key institutional investors.

BillDesk (IndiaIdeas.com Limited)                                                                     BillDesk provides Payment aggregation &
                                                                                                      Electronic Bill Payment services, with FY25
BillDesk, was founded on March 29, 2000, by M.N. Srinivasu, Ajay Kaushal, and Karthik Ganapathy
                                                                                                      revenue at Rs23bn
and is headquartered in Mumbai. BillDesk provides payment aggregation and Electronic Bill
Presentment and Payment services to large enterprise and government clients, with nationwide
operations supported by integrations across all commercial banks and thousands of utility service
providers.

The company received a Cross-Border Payment Aggregator license from the RBI in July 2024,
enabling export and import-linked payment processing. Recurring payments form the largest
revenue stream, contributing approximately 50% of total revenue, while loyalty management
services account for around 16%. By payment mode, more than 60% of transactions are processed
through UPI and net banking, with e-wallets and card payments together comprising 30-35% of the
transaction mix.

As of FY24, BillDesk processed over 4bn transactions annually and handled approximately 150mn
Application Programming Interface calls per day. The platform connects more than 20,000 active
billers across 27+ states and maintains an estimated 60% market share in online bill payments.
Key operating metrics include a take rate or merchant discount rate of 0.3% on a Total Payment
Volume of Rs10trn in FY24.

Financial performance moderated during FY24, with revenue at Rs23bn, reflecting a 13% YoY
decline. EBITDA margin stood at 5%, while profit after tax was Rs1bn, down 14.6% YoY. Over
FY22-24, revenue grew at a CAGR of 2.3%, while profit after tax recorded a CAGR of 10%.

BillDesk last raised $85mn in a Series D funding round led by Visa at a valuation of $1.6bn in
2019. In 2021, Prosus NV cancelled a $4.7bn deal to buy BillDesk. The shareholder base comprises
private equity and venture capital investors holding a combined 57%, including General Atlantic, TA
Associates, and Clearstone, while the founders hold 30%. Visa owns a 13% stake, and Temasek
holds 8%.

OneCard (FPL Technologies Private Limited)                                                              OneCard runs a co-branded credit card & a
                                                                                                        credit score monitoring app, with Rs19bn
OneCard was founded in February 2019 by Anurag Sinha, Rupesh Kumar, and Vibhav Hathi, and
                                                                                                        revenue in FY25
is headquartered in Pune, Maharashtra, with Anurag Sinha serving as CEO. It operates across
two core products: OneCard, a co-branded credit card issued in partnership with multiple banks
and OneScore, a credit score monitoring application used during customer acquisition process.
Operations are India-focused, with underwriting and customer sourcing concentrated on digitally
acquired prime borrowers.

OneCard's revenue is driven by a) interchange income sharing, contributing 60-70% of revenues,
b) interest income sharing at 15-20%, and c) fees and charges accounting for 10%. Partner banks
include Federal Bank, IDFC First Bank, Bank of Baroda, CSB Bank, South Indian Bank, and Indian
Bank as of late 2024. OneCard serves over 70mn users on the OneScore platform and a total
employee base of 1,005. It is focused on prime borrowers with credit scores above 750 sourced
via OneScore, while OneCard Lite is offered as an FD-backed product for users with credit scores
below 750, enabling credit access while limiting risk exposure. In Dec-25, the RBI has instructed its
partner banks to halt new card issuance and has sought clarity on data-sharing norms in these co-
branded credit card arrangements.

FY25 financial performance continued growth alongside improving loss metrics amid regulatory
constraints. Revenue stood at Rs18.8bn in FY25, increasing 32% YoY from Rs14.3bn in FY24. Over
FY22-25, revenue increased at a CAGR of 182%, scaling from Rs0.8bn in FY22. EBITDA margin
improved to -15.7% in FY25 from -67.6% in FY23, translating into EBITDA losses of Rs2.9bn in FY25
(vs Rs4bn, FY24). Losses have narrowed over FY23-25. Net loss narrowed to -Rs3bn in FY25 from
-Rs4bn in FY24.

The latest valuation was set in the Series D extension round in November 2024, which raised
$28.5mn led by Peak XV, Z47, and Better Tomorrow at a post-money valuation of c.Rs117bn
($1.4bn), following the Series D round in July 2022 led by Temasek at a valuation of c.Rs104bn. The
cap table comprises founders holding 28.5% (with Anurag Sinha at 16%), Peak XV at 22%, Matrix
and Z47 jointly at 17%, and an ESOP pool of 3%.

Juspay, founded in 2012 by Vimal Kumar (CEO) and Ramanathan RV, is headquartered in                    Juspay offers a universal payment ops
Bengaluru and operates as a universal payment operating system. The company provides a                 system with revenue of Rs5bn (90% via
technology orchestration layer that sits upstream of payment gateways, enabling intelligent routing,   payment platform integration fees)
authentication, and seamless user experience across digital payments. Company is expanding into
Payment Aggregator segment.

Juspay’s core product suite includes HyperSDK for native in-app payment pages, Express Checkout
for dynamic transaction routing, HyperUPI for cloud-native banking infrastructure, and the open-
source Hyperswitch platform. Revenue is largely driven by payment platform integration fees, which
contributed Rs4.7bn in FY25, i.e., 92% of overall revenues.

The company has strengthened its positioning in India’s digital payments ecosystem through
strategic initiatives, including the acquisition of Lotus Pay to expand recurring payments
capabilities and the receipt of a Payment Aggregator license from the RBI in early 2024.
Operationally, Juspay processes an annualized TPV of approximately $1tn (up 150% YoY) and
supports over 300mn daily transactions for over 500 enterprise clients. HyperSDK is installed on
more than 250mn devices and is used by large enterprise clients such as Amazon India, Flipkart,
Swiggy, and Uber.

In 2024, Juspay secured license from RBI to operate as a Payment Aggregator. As per CNBC (March
25, 2025), select payments platforms like Paytm & Cashfree among others have partly reduced
partnership with Juspay. This may be reflection of PA/ PG seeking to directly service their clients
as well as access to client data.

In FY25, revenue rose over 60% YoY to Rs5bn and grew at a 66% Cagr over FY20-25. The company
turned positive at adj EBITDA (ex-ESOPs) level that stood at Rs919mn in FY25, with a 23% EBITDA
margin. PAT was reported at Rs622mn in FY25, following losses in the preceding years. Revenue
growth outpaced expense growth, driven by higher automation levels and the spin-off of the
Namma Yatri business, contributing to improved profitability.

Juspay was last valued at Rs106bn ($1.24bn) following a $60mn Series D funding round in April
2025 led by Kedaara Capital. The shareholding structure comprises institutional investors holding
41%, founders holding 27%, and an ESOP pool of 16%. Key institutional shareholders include Accel
(12%), VEF (10%), and SoftBank (7-11%).

Cashfree Payments was founded in 2015 by Akash Sinha and Reeju Datta and is headquartered
                                                                                                                                      FY25 revenues of Rs6.4bn
in Bengaluru. Akash Sinha serves as the CEO. The company operates a full-stack payments
and Application Programming Interface banking platform, offering solutions across payment
collections, payouts, banking-as-a-service, and cross-border payments.

Cashfree has secured Payment Aggregator, Payment Aggregator-Cross Border, and Prepaid
Payment Instrument licenses. From an operational standpoint, the platform processes an
annualized transaction volume of approximately $80bn and supports peak throughput of up to
12,000 transactions per second.

The platform has built a broad merchant footprint, serving over 800,000 businesses as of FY25,
including enterprise clients such as Zomato, Nykaa, and Swiggy. The company has also expanded
internationally through its UAE arm, targeting growth across the Middle East and North Africa
region.

Financial performance was relatively stable in FY25, with revenue at Rs6.4bn (flat YoY). Cashfree’s
revenue is primarily driven by payment gateway revenues, which contributed Rs5bn in FY25,
followed by contributions from other services at Rs1bn and payouts at Rs0.5bn. Over FY22-25,
revenue expanded at a CAGR of 41%. It reported a net loss of Rs1.5bn in FY25 (vs loss of Rs1.3bn
in FY24). Adjusted Ebitda was negative at Rs1.3bn in FY25 (-20% margin), vs Rs1.1bn and a margin
of -17% in FY24. The increase in losses was driven by higher engineering and compliance costs
incurred during a period of regulatory restrictions on new merchant onboarding.

The latest valuation for Cashfree stands at Rs61bn ($700mn) following a $53mn Series C funding
round completed in February 2025, led by KRAFTON with participation from Apis Partners. The
shareholder base also includes State Bank of India and Y Combinator.

EaseBuzz Private Limited                                                                                                              EaseBuzz operates a software-enabled
                                                                                                                                      payments biz. & focuses on collection
EaseBuzz Private Limited was founded in 2014 by Rohit Prasad (MD & CEO) and is headquartered in
                                                                                                                                      journeys with Rs7bn revenue in FY25
Pune. Amit Kumar is the co-founder of the business and serves as the CTO. The company operates
a software-enabled payments business, offering payment aggregation along with embedded
financial workflow solutions targeted at education, government collections, and B2B enterprises
across India. It focuses on collection journeys and has a stronger presence in segments like
education (historically strong focus), NBFCs & insurance, retail (selective, solution-led), B2B supply-
chain-driven businesses; it has recently ventured into real estate, municipal corporations for
property payments.

Easebuzz’s product portfolio includes FeesBuzz, a fee collection and enterprise resource planning
platform for educational institutions, and Teller, a B2B accounts receivable and invoice-to-cash
automation solution built on Bharat Connect and Bharat Bill Payment System infrastructure.
Revenue is primarily driven by transaction processing fees and SaaS components, with scale
supported by diversified merchant use cases. In FY24, the company exited gaming ahead
of regulatory scrutiny, stopped corporate-card/rewards-driven enterprise programs, which were
volume-heavy but low-quality and price-driven. Instead, it focused on scaling revenue sustainably.
Easebuzz has consciously avoided or exited the following segments: Travel, airlines, hotels, highly
price-sensitive & low-margin sectors, large-scale retail marketplaces without solution complexity.

During FY25, Easebuzz processed approximately $30bn in Gross Transaction Value, with
average daily volumes of around 1mn transactions, and served more than 200k merchants.
FeesBuzz was deployed across over 10,000 institutions, reflecting strong penetration within
the education segment. The company strengthened its regulatory position by securing RBI
authorizations for Payment Aggregator-Online, Payment Aggregator-Physical, and Cross-Border
Payment Aggregator. Easebuzz also launched the Teller platform toward the end of FY24 and into

Innoviti Payment Solutions                                                                                                            Innoviti operates across online, offline, and
                                                                                                                                      UPI payment channels, with FY25 revenues
Innoviti, founded in 2002 by Rajeev Agrawal (CEO) and Amrita Malik, is headquartered in Bengaluru.
                                                                                                                                      of Rs1.4bn
Innoviti operates across India’s diverse payment ecosystem - spanning online, offline, and UPI
channels - where it has historically built its strengths through a retail-first approach. Its key
products include UniPay for enterprises, Genie for mid-market electronics retailers, and Link
for SMEs, collectively serving ~80,000 counters with industry-leading reliability and software
differentiation. Management believes that by layering intelligence on top of payment flows, the
company strengthens retailer economics through revenue assurance (money gets credited to bank
account), promotions, and cash-flow optimization.

Genie caters to the mid-markets serving mobile & electronics retail (Samsung/Vivo dealers etc.)
across 10k counters. Link is an asset-light solution for high-value remote payments, focused on
improving merchant cash flows. It has 50k+ downloads with ~8k active counters due to eligibility
limits, but is seeing fast growth in EMI-based payments, especially among small merchants looking
to avoid card swipe costs.

The company received its RBI Online Payment Aggregator license in Mar 2024 and holds a higher
market share in the enterprise category. It operates at 80k counters dominated by the enterprise
clients (75-80% of counters). It processes over Rs800bn in annual purchase volume for clients such
as Reliance Retail, Tanishq, Pantaloon, Zudio, McDonald among others. It does provide services
around EMI on cards and is also focusing on customer acquisition for lenders as well.

In FY25, operating revenue grew 35% YoY to Rs1.4bn, driven by SaaS monetization. Its revenue
grew at a Cagr of 24% over FY22-25. Innoviti's losses at adj EBITDA level has consistently narrowed
and stood at -Rs231mn in FY25 (vs -Rs305mn, FY24).

Google Pay was incorporated on January 25, 2017, as a wholly owned subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. In                                   Google Pay is a TPAP in India’s UPI
India, the company, headquartered in New Delhi, is led by Preeti Lobana (Country Manager). Google                                   ecosystem with a 36% market share (Sep-25)
Pay operates as a third-party application provider (TPAP) India’s UPI ecosystem. As on Sept-25,                                     & FY25 revenue of Rs15bn
it commands a c.36% market share of UPI transaction value and serves more than 67mn active
users. As of FY25, 30% of Google India Digital's revenues were from overseas.

Monetization is routed through indirect revenue streams, including merchant services such as
SoundPod hardware subscriptions and the distribution of consumer credit products, including
small-ticket or sachet loans. On the regulatory front, the National Payments Corporation of
India extended the deadline for adherence to the 30% UPI market share cap to December 31,
2026, providing additional runway to manage market concentration. In parallel, Google Pay has
accelerated the rollout of SoundPod devices to expand its merchant footprint and compete more
aggressively in offline acceptance infrastructure.

Financial performance in FY25 reflects modest top-line growth and drop of 5pp YoY in adj. Ebitda
margins. Revenue stood at Rs15bn in FY25, up 3% YoY, while PAT declined 56% YoY to Rs0.5bn.
Adj. Ebitda amounted to Rs0.7bn in FY25, with margins down to 5% (vs 10%, FY24) on higher opex.
Net margins saw an improving trend over FY22-24 before declining to 3% in FY25. Over FY22-25,
revenue grew at a Cagr of 7%. The company remains profitable, indicating franchise strength
despite regulatory constraints on revenue growth. Google retains 100% of the equity.

Payments Banks in India                                                                                                                          Payments Bank were established by RBI to
                                                                                                                                                 support digital payments and drive financial
Payments Bank license were offered by RBI with an objective to leverage a combination of digital
                                                                                                                                                 inclusion
platforms, with banking license to support digital payments and drive financial inclusion. Banks
operate an asset-light “Phygital” model, combining a physical merchant network with digital banking
solutions to serve the unbanked and underbanked population through products such as Domestic
Money Transfer (DMT), Micro-ATMs, and Current Account Savings Account (CASA) subscriptions
and Cash Management Services (CMS).

There were certain restrictions imposed on these banks including restriction from making loans
and corporate bonds and limiting deposit relationship at Rs0.2m. The sector has requested hike in
this limit to Rs0.5m. In this backdrop, these banks mostly raise deposits through savings deposits
(100% of deposits) & deploy in government securities. In fact, the majority of their income is made
through fees (40-90% of total income). During FY25, cost/ income ratio of companies in the sector
is higher at 80-90% and ROA at 1-2% and ROE at 10-12%. The segment has total deposit base of
Rs250bn, grown at 48% Cagr over past three years, but overall share in total deposits is low at 0.1%
& 0.4% in savings deposits.

India Post Payment Bank Limited                                                                                                    IPPB earns revenue from trx & service fees,
                                                                                                                                   distribution commissions, & deposit float
India Post Payments Bank was established in 2018 under the Department of Posts, Ministry of
                                                                                                                                   income, with FY25 NII of Rs8bn
Communications. The bank is led by Mr. R. Viswesvaran, Managing Director and CEO. Operations
are pan-India spanning approximately 0.16m post offices. IPPB continues to operate with 100%
equity ownership by the Government of India. Government of India stated that IPPB will not convert
into a Small Finance Bank.

IPPB’s revenue is driven by a) transaction-based fees and service charges, b) commissions
from distribution of third-party credit, insurance, and pension products, and c) float income from
deposits deployed in permitted investments. As of August 2025, the bank had a customer base
exceeding 120mn and total deposits of approximately Rs200bn. Lending is executed through
partner institutions including HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, Aditya Birla Capital Finance, and Aadhaar
Housing Finance, with no lending risk retained on IPPB’s balance sheet.

Financially, total income stood at Rs18bn in FY25, compared with Rs11bn in FY24. Net profit was
Rs1.3bn in FY25 and Rs340mn in FY24, compared with losses till FY22. It generated ROE of 10%
in FY25.

Airtel Payments Bank Limited                                                                                                      Airtel Payments Bank offers digital savings
                                                                                                                                  a/c, remittance services, & CMS with NII
Airtel Payments Bank, founded by Bharti Airtel and headquartered in Gurugram, offers digital
                                                                                                                                  Rs2bn in FY25
savings accounts, remittance services, and institutional Cash Management Services (CMS). Led by
MD & CEO Anubrata Biswas, the bank leverages a phygital network of over 0.5m banking points
to earn revenue through transaction commissions and CMS fees. Positioned as a “Safe Second
Account” to mitigate digital fraud risks, it digitizes over Rs80bn of cash monthly for more than 4,000
corporate clients.

In March 2025, Bharti Airtel restructured its holdings by transferring its 70% direct stake to Airtel
Limited to consolidate digital assets. The bank also partnered with Noise to launch payment-
enabled smartwatches. Operating metrics show a customer base of over 150mn and an annualized
revenue run rate of Rs32bn as of 2QFY26.

As on Mar-25, bank had deposit balance of Rs34bn, up 30% YoY. It generated revenues of Rs26bn
of which large majority originated from fees. PAT rose 81% YoY to Rs630mn. For 2QFY26, revenue
was Rs8bn and EBITDA Rs893mn, implying an EBITDA margin of 11%.

Jio Payments Bank Limited                                                                                                 Jio PB primarily earns revenue from treasury
                                                                                                                          income due to lending restrictions
Jio Payments Bank, founded in 2018 as a joint venture between Reliance Industries Ltd and SBI,
offers digital savings accounts, current accounts, and bill payments through a phygital model
across India. The bank primarily earns revenue from treasury income on government securities due
to lending restrictions, with operations supported by the Jio Finance App and a network of over
14,000 business correspondents.

In May 2024, the bank launched the Jio Finance App, and in June 2025, Jio Financial Services
acquired SBI’s 18% stake, making the bank a wholly owned subsidiary. The Jio Finance app has
introduced a feature that allows users to compare and invest in FDs offered by multiple banks
and NBFCs on a single platform. The company said that users can now access FDs from lenders
including Unity SFB, Suryoday SFB, Utkarsh SFB, BAF, Shriram, and MMFS through the app. As of
Mar-26, it reported +60% YoY rise to 3.7mn in casa customers, 378k business correspondents, and
deposits reaching Rs5.4bn by Mar-26.

In FY26, it had deposits of Rs5bn, rising from Rs3bn a year ago. In FY25, NII was flat YoY at Rs0.1,
while the company reported a loss of Rs1bn. The entity was valued at c.Rs5.9bn ($66mn) during
the June 2025 stake acquisition by Jio Financial Services, which now holds 100% equity.

LendTech                                                                                                                      Over the next five years, the LendTech should
                                                                                                                              see 22% Cagr in loans
India's Fintech lending platforms have built a book of Rs2.1tn (US$25bn) as on Mar-25, growing
35% YoY/ 18% Cagr over FY20-25 and making up 1% of total credit. FinTechs dominate the small
ticket personal loan (STPL - ticket size less than Rs50,000) space, contributing to 86% of industry
origination, and the segment forms 8% of retail consumers. Within the total FinTech originations,
91% were of small ticket personal loans. Loan against property and lower ticket business loans
have seen a rise, showing that lenders are also diversifying into other products to meet consumer
demands. In fact, 17% of industry originations in business loans in 4QFY25 were by FinTechs. This
segment of lenders had faced higher pressure on their asset quality in the STPL segment, but it is
interesting to note that trends have been showing improvement. The key to watch will be trends in
their business loans. Over the next five years, the segment should see 22% Cagr in loans aided by
customer acquisition and this can lift the loan book to more than doubling in next five years. This
should aid growth in revenues as well as improvement in profitability.

Key risks in this sector can be from two areas; first risk can be from regulatory intervention on
capping of interest rates/fees that tend to be much higher than banks and traditional NBFCs, while
second risk can be from any deterioration in collection efforts or asset quality as the ticket size of
these loans is quite small that makes collection costs significantly more costly in the context of
principal at risk.

Ugro Capital                                                                                                                                                                                  Ugro Capital operates as an MSME-focused
                                                                                                                                                                                              NBFC with Revenues at Rs19bn & PAT of
Ugro Capital Limited started in 2018 after Shachindra Nath acquired Chokhani Securities Limited.
                                                                                                                                                                                              Rs1.7bn in FY26
The company is headquartered in Mumbai, and Anuj Pandey serves as CEO. UGRO operates as an
MSME-focused NBFC, using cash-flow based underwriting through its GRO Score framework and
running a Lending-as-a-Service model. Revenue is primarily driven by interest income from on-book
loans, while fee and assignment income is generated through off-book co-lending and partnerships.

AUM stood at Rs153bn in FY26, reflecting 28%YoY growth. Off-book AUM accounted for 38%
of total AUM. The platform is supported by +16 co-lending partners and works with +59 lenders
and more than 60 fintech partners. AUM sourcing is diversified, led by Prime Branch Led at
53%, Emerging Markets at 25%, Ecosystem at 12%, and Partnerships at 14%. Lending exposure
spans Healthcare, Education, Chemicals, Food Processing, Hospitality, Auto Components, and
Light Engineering.

Recent updates include the all-cash acquisition of Profectus Capital for Rs14bn and the integration
of MyShubhLife to scale embedded finance. In the 4QFY26, the company saw borrowing cost
at 10.2%, net disbursements of Rs21bn, GNPA at 2.5% (2.2%, 3Q), NNPA at 1.6%, and collection
efficiency at 98% (99%, 3Q).

Revenue rose 39% YoY to Rs19bn in FY26 (vs Rs14bn, FY25), implying a 58% Cagr growth over
FY22-26. PAT rose 21% YoY to Rs1.7bn in FY26 (vs Rs1.4bn, FY24). The company has been
profitable over the last 5 years with PAT margins expanding over FY22-26 to 9% in FY26.

The latest market capitalization stands at Rs15bn (US$158mn) as of Jul-26 & the shareholding
structure reflects Promoter and Group ownership at 2%, FIIs at 23% led by NewQuest Asia, PAG,
and ADV Partners, and Public and Others at 74%.

                                                                                                                                             (group entity), alongside DMI Housing
DMI Finance Pvt. Ltd was founded in 2008 in New Delhi by Shivashish Chatterjee and Yuvraja C.
                                                                                                                                             Finance (DHFPL)
Singh, who serve as Joint Managing Directors. Arindam Das is the CEO. The company (DFPL) is a
subsidiary of DMI Limited (group entity), alongside DMI Housing Finance (DHFPL). DFPL operates
as a digital lending NBFC offering personal loans, consumption loans, MSME loans, and loans

As of Sept-25, DMI group's AUM stood at Rs85bn consisting of 70% consumer loans, 25%
affordable housing finance loans, and 4% wholesale real estate loans. Its home loan book is
geographically diversified across states with UP, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh accounting
for 50% of the HL book. The group’s borrowing profile included FIs at 51%, securitisation 12%,
debentures 25%, direct assignments 11% and CP 1%. Its loan book witnessed a significant run-down
in Sept-25 due to decline in disbursements despite the lifting of the restrictions on the sanction and
disbursal of loans by the RBI in Jan-25. Operating metrics highlight 25mn customers and a network
of 85,000 Samsung retail stores.

The DMI group’s profitability weakened in FY25, with RoMA at 0.3% compared to 3.3% in FY24. This
decline was due to higher opex from larger collections teams, added infrastructure and increased
IT costs at a subsidiary, along with higher credit costs driven by elevated write-offs in the consumer
book. DFPL reported a net loss of ~Rs277mn in FY25 (vs profits of Rs4,032mn, FY24). As of Sep-25,
the gross stage 3 increased to 5.9% (vs 4% in Mar-25) due to lumpy exposures in the corporate
loan segment and the base effect from the run-down in consumer loans. Its CRAR was 74% on a
net worth of Rs68bn as of Sep-25.

As of Sept-25, DHFPL’s loan book stood at Rs21bn (vs Rs19bn, Mar-25), with home loans 72% of
the book, LAP 28% and others formed 0.3%. Its gross stage 3 rose to 1.1% as of Sep-25, vs 0.7% in
Mar-25. DHFPL reported PAT of Rs710mn in FY25 (vs Rs530mn in FY24), while its RoMA was 3%
in FY25 (2.9% in FY24) supported by stable NIMs, controlled credit costs and higher non-interest
income. In H1FY26, RoMA declined to 2.6% due to NIM compression from lower average yields
and higher opex, although credit costs remained controlled. Its CRAR was 74% on a net worth of
Rs11bn as of Mar-25.

The latest valuation is Rs252bn (US$3bn) following a US$334mn (Rs28bn) fundraise in Aug 2024
led by MUFG Bank. DFPL's shareholding comprises DMI Limited (Mauritius) at 69%, MUFG Bank at
18-20%, and NIS Ganesha at 10%. DHFPL used to be a subsidiary of DFPL (till FY18), DMI Limited,
Mauritius now directly holds 81% in DHFPL as on Sept-25, followed by DMI Income Fund Pte Ltd
(12.67%).

Navi Technologies Limited                                                                                                         Navi operates in lending, general insurance,
                                                                                                                                  and asset management
Navi, founded in 2018 by Sachin Bansal and Ankit Agarwal with Rajiv Naresh as the CEO
and headquartered in Bengaluru. The company operates in lending, general insurance, and
asset management. Its lending arm, Navi Finserv, is the primary revenue driver with a portfolio
concentrated 87% in unsecured personal loans and 13% in home loans, as of FY25.

In Oct 2024, RBI temporarily halted new loan sanctions, lifting the restriction in Dec 2024. Navi
recently divested Chaitanya India Fin Credit for Rs15bn to pivot fully to digital lending. It has a 2.8%
UPI volume market share, processing 260mn transactions in Feb 2025.

In FY25, net revenue from operations rose 16% YoY to Rs17bn. It reported a net loss of Rs1.3bn,
compared to a positive PAT of Rs1.7bn due to higher other income in FY24. Net revenue grew
at a 27% CAGR over FY22-25. GNPA/NNPA moderated to 2.23%/ 0.31% as of Jun-25 (vs. 2.53%/
0.35% in Mar-25; 1.94%/ 0.15% in Mar-24), though adjusted 90+ dpd remains elevated at ~6.8%
(vs 6.9% in Mar-25; 5.4% in Mar-24), while home loan delinquencies remain low at ~0.6%. Going
forward the company aims to focus on secured lending and better selection of borrowers through
the underwriting models, stringent approval rates & tight monitoring and collection systems.

The company was valued at Rs151bn ($1.7bn) as of Sep 2025, with total equity funding of $445mn
raised primarily from the promoter and Gaja Capital. Sachin Bansal & the founding team retains
99% shareholding.

Moneyview Limited                                                                                                                         Moneyview runs a digital lending model,
                                                                                                                                          combining a marketplace with its own
Moneyview, formerly Whizdm Innovations Private Limited, headquartered in Bengaluru, was
                                                                                                                                          balance sheet lending
founded in 2014 by Puneet Agarwal (CEO) and Sanjay Aggarwal. The company operates a full-
stack digital lending model combining a marketplace platform with balance sheet lending through
its subsidiary Whizdm Finance. Product offerings include personal loans, co-branded credit cards,
motor insurance, and secured loans against property. Revenue is driven by fees and commissions,
which contributed +60% of operating revenue in FY25, alongside interest income. India Ratings
upgrades the credit rating to IND A-/Stable citing sustained profitability, stable asset quality and
prudent leverage as key supporting drivers.

As on Mar-25, total AUM were at Rs167bn, with the NBFC book at Rs43bn, and 75% of users located
in Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets. Recent developments include the acquisition of earned wage access
platform Jify in Sep-24 and conversion to a public limited company in mid-2025. Operating metrics
show 200mn+ registered users and a 58% repeat rate as of Mar-25.

In FY25, net revenue rose by 122% YoY to Rs20bn from Rs9bn in FY24, delivering a 102% Cagr over
FY22-25. PAT rose over 40% YoY to Rs2.4bn (Rs1.7bn, FY24), with net profit margins improving to
10% in FY25 from 7% in FY22.

On a consolidated basis, Moneyview reported PAT of Rs2.4bn in FY25, up ~40% YoY. Return on
avg AUM stood at c.1.8% in FY25. Credit costs remained stable at c.5.7% during the year, while the
pre-provision operating profit buffer improved to ~1.31x, supporting profitability through the credit
cycle. Consolidated leverage stood at c.2.6x in FY25, with tangible net worth of ~Rs18bn. The NBFC
subsidiary (Whizdm FInance) reported a CAR of c.24% in FY25.

The latest valuation was Rs101bn (US$1.2bn) following a $4.65mn internal bridge round in Sep-24
led by Accel and Nexus. Shareholding includes founders at 24%, Accel Partners at 22%, and Tiger
Global at 12%.
