Oxyzo Financial Services Limited                                                                                                 Oxyzo operates an MSME-focused NBFC
                                                                                                                                 with NII at Rs8bn & PAT of Rs3.4bn in FY25
Oxyzo, founded in 2016 by Ruchi Kalra (CEO), Asish Mohapatra, and team is headquartered
in Gurugram. The company provides secured B2B purchase financing and financing solutions
embedded in supply chains, primarily serving manufacturing and infrastructure sectors with a
portfolio that is 67% secured. Oxyzo operates across 20+ states with growing presence in southern/
western clusters.

Revenue diversification comes through its Ziel micro-lending division, Supply Chain Finance for
infrastructure, and fixed-income products. Recently, Ziel scaled to 100+ branches, introduced fixed-
income pilots for corporate treasuries, and executed securitization transactions. As of Mar-26, it
has over 10,000 active customers and AUM of Rs118bn.

In FY25, net revenue grew 34% YoY to Rs12bn, while PAT rose 45% YoY to Rs3.4bn. Net revenues
delivered a 65% Cagr over FY22-25, with profits improving at 70% Cagr over FY22-25. GS3 has
remained stable across FY24-25 and reduced to 1% as of 1QFY26. ROEs have sustained and stood
at ~12% in FY25 on improving yields & lower opex. CRAR for the company stood at 36.5% as on
1QFY26.

The company was valued at Rs80bn ($0.9bn) in its Mar-22 Series A round, raising US$200mn led
by Alpha Wave Global and Tiger Global. Shareholding is controlled by parent OfBusiness (OFB Tech
Pvt. Ltd.) at ~70%, followed by Alpha Wave Global (7%) and Tiger Global (5%).

Mintifi Finserve Private Limited                                                                                                    Mintifi operates as NBFC focused on supply
                                                                                                                                    chain financing for SMEs with NII at Rs3.6bn
Mintifi was founded in 2017 by Anup Agarwal (CEO), Sanjoy Shome, and Ankit Mehta and is
                                                                                                                                    & PAT of Rs1bn in FY25
headquartered in Mumbai. The company operates as NBFC focused on supply chain financing
for SMEs, where credit underwriting is based on transaction-level flow data sourced from large
corporate anchors through enterprise resource planning systems integrations. Minitifi offers
revolving supply chain credit lines, short term working capital loans, loans against property, and
factoring services, with closed-loop disbursement directly to anchors and collections supported
by stop-supply arrangements. Revenue is primarily driven from interest income (80% of the FY24
Revenues), processing fees, and sale of goods (20%).

The company launched secured lending through loans against property in 2024, received an RBI
factoring license enabling outright purchase of receivables, and intimated technology monetization
through supply chain and dealer management software offered to corporate partners.

The company's AUM stood at Rs29bn spread across 3 segments: Supply chain financing (90% of
AUM), term loans (7%) & loans against property (3%). Avg tick size for the book was c.Rs1.4mn.
In FY25, net revenue was at Rs3.6bn, up 45% YoY, implying a Cagr of 118% over FY22-25. PAT
stood at Rs714mn in FY25, growing at +160% Cagr over FY23-25 on better operational efficiency,
financial leverage and lower taxes.

The latest funding round was Series E in November 2024, with the company valued at Rs73bn
(US$850mn), led by Ontario Teachers' Pension plan and Prosus. Other Key shareholders include
Norwest Venture Partners, Premji Invest, Elevation Capital, IFC, and Growth Catalyst Partners.

Kissht (OnEMI Technology Solutions Limited)                                                                                          Kissht provides unsecured personal loans of
                                                                                                                                     up to Rs0.5mn, with FY25 NII of Rs12bn &
Kissht, founded in 2015 by Krishnan Vishwanathan and Ranvir Singh, operates a vertically
                                                                                                                                     PAT of Rs2bn
integrated fintech ecosystem led by CEO Krishnan Vishwanathan. The company runs a two-engine
model comprising Ring, a transactional credit and payments app with 53mn registered users, and
Kissht, a monetization engine offering personal loans up to Rs0.5mn to credit-tested users, besides
some secured loans.

Kissht is one of the few new-age digital lending players that is deploying “credit QR” based offline-
to-online (O2O) customer acquisition model in India. Revenue is driven by interest income and
processing fees, with AUM of Rs41bn as of FY25, of which 98% is unsecured and 60% of loans
are on-book. As of Mar-25, it serves over 9mn unique customers, with average age slightly up to
32 years.

In FY26, it reported a net revenue of Rs19bn, down 62% YoY & net profit of Rs2.8bn (75% YoY).
Over FY22-26, net revenue grew at a CAGR of ~40%, while PAT transitioned from losses in FY21
to sustained profitability FY22 onward, demonstrating improving operating leverage despite near-
term moderation. The company's ROA rose in FY26 due to higher net income, but was partially
offset by higher opex & provisions. Gross stage 3 fell to 2.12% (2.9% in FY25), with PCR down to
86% from 91% in FY25. Its CAR was stable at 25% as on Mar-26.

As of Sept-24, the company was valued at Rs25bn ($294mn) and it last raised $80mn in a Series
E round in Jun 2022 led by Vertex Growth and Brunei Investment Agency. Shareholding is led by
Promoters (31%), Vertex Ventures (23%), and Ventureast (9%).

Slice Small Finance Bank Limited (merged with North East Small Finance Bank)                                                           Slice SFB aims to build a digital bank for
                                                                                                                                       India, with AUM of ~Rs45bn (Mar-26), ~79%
Slice, based out of Bengaluru, was initially launched by Rajan Bajaj as a digital consumer lending
                                                                                                                                       in unsecured loans
platform targeting students and young professionals with app-led short-tenure credit and card-
based offerings. In September 2023, RBI permitted the merger of slice with North East Small
Finance Bank. The merger was completed in October 2024, following which the entity was renamed
Slice Small Finance Bank.

Post-merger, it aims to build a digital bank for India. As of Mar-26, Slice SFB's AUM stood at
~Rs45bn. Unsecured loans of ~Rs36bn accounted for ~79% of the book and secured loans of
Rs10bn made up the remaining ~21%. It has pan-India digital reach while physical branches remain
concentrated in the Northeast. The company consciously moderated its growth to strengthen risk,
governance and regulatory systems. Now management is targeting ~30% Cagr growth sustainably,
alongside a long-term opportunity in fee income in the next 10-15 years.

Slice's merchant offering combines high-frequency UPI payments and embedded unsecured
credit for a base of ~65mn merchants. The platform differentiates through same-day payment
settlements for merchants (vs next-day industry standard) and consumer payments routed via
RuPay credit cards linked to UPI. No-cost EMI options drive ~5-6x higher acceptance than plastic
cards. This payments-plus-credit model deepens merchant engagement while supporting scalable
fee-led growth.

In FY26, it reported pre-ESOP PAT of over Rs1bn in its first profitable phase, driven by improved                                      Driving operating leverage & targeting
NIMs, lower opex and range-bound credit costs. Total income rose to Rs14bn vs Rs6bn in FY25.                                           sub-30% C/I ratio, aided by branch light ops
NIMs as of FY26 was 10.7% as compared to 10.6% in FY25. It is driving operating leverage, targeting
a sub-30% C/I ratio, aided by branch-light ops saving ~50-70bps on costs. On the balance sheet,
deposits rose to Rs51bn in FY26 and advances to Rs45bn. Net NPA declined to 3.67% in FY26 from
4.67% in FY25. As on Mar'26, the company's gross net worth stood at ~Rs9.5bn.

The latest disclosed valuation in June 2022 was at c.Rs120bn (US$1.5bn). Key shareholders include
Gunosy Capital, Blume Ventures, Tiger Global, Insight Partners, and founder Rajan Bajaj.

Branch International Inc.                                                                                                       Branch International operates as an NBFC
                                                                                                                                offering unsecured PLs, with NII at Rs7bn
Branch International Inc. was founded in 2015 by Matt Flannery (CEO) and Daniel Jung, and is
                                                                                                                                and PAT of Rs1bn
headquartered in San Francisco. The company operates a digital lending and neobanking model
across India, Kenya, Nigeria and Tanzania, primarily offering unsecured personal loans. Branch
International Financial Services Pvt Ltd (BIFSPL), a wholly owned sub of Branch Intnl Inc, is led by
Neeraj Gupta, who serves as the MD & CEO. It operates as an NBFC in India (contributes to 90% of
global revenues), a licensed finance company in Nigeria, and a majority shareholder in a regulated
microfinance bank in Kenya. The Indian entity, founded in 2019, offers digital personal loans ranging
from Rs1k-200k with repayment periods of up to two years.

Revenues are driven by interest income (50% of FY25 revenues) and fee income (50%). It has
recently acquired Century Microfinance Bank in Kenya, allowing Branch to mobilize low-cost
deposits and reduce funding dependence on wholesale debt. The company is also integrating Gen
AI to create synthetic data for risk modelling, building on its traditional device-data underwriting
approach.

Operating metrics for India show AUM at Rs13bn (100% unsecured PLs) as of Sept-25 (vs Rs9bn,
FY25), with 0% GNPA due to conservative write-off policies. Disbursements rose to Rs63bn in
Sept-25, after rising 148% YoY to Rs51bn in FY25. FY25 total income stood at Rs8bn (146% YoY),
50% of which is driven by interest income and remaining comes from fees. Opex rose over 140%
YoY on back of higher marketing costs, while credit costs were high at ~45% of FY25 total income.
PAT grew 46% YoY to Rs1bn in FY25 (vs Rs0.7bn, FY24), though RoAA and RoNW moderated due
to rapid balance sheet expansion and equity infusion.

In Feb-22, BIFSPL's parent entity raised US$300mn on a post-money valuation of Rs290bn (US
$4bn). The cap table (at the US parent level) incl. founders and key management, alongside major
venture investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Foundation Capital, Trinity Ventures, and strategic
investors including Visa and B Capital, with IFC and Khosla Impact representing impact-focused
capital. Debt providers include Victory Park Capital and Greenspring. The parent company holds
100% equity in its operating subsidiaries, centralizing ownership at the U.S. level.

Truebalance (Balancehero India)                                                                                             Truebalance offers unsecured short-term
                                                                                                                            personal loans, with FY25 NII at Rs8bn and
Truebalance headquartered in Gurugram, was founded in 2014 by Charlie Lee (CEO). The company
                                                                                                                            PAT of Rs1bn
operates a digital consumer lending platform focused on under-banked and new-to-credit users
across India, with unsecured short-term personal loans as its core product. Lending is conducted
by its RBI-licensed NBFC subsidiary.

Truebalance transitioned from a consumer utility application to a lending-led model, with unsecured
short-tenure personal loans forming the core offering. Revenue is driven by retail lending,
with revenue generated primarily from interest income and loan processing fees. Lending is
digitally originated and concentrated in tier-2/3 regions. Truebalance offers unsecured cash loans
(Rs5-100k), complemented by Level Up Loans, a smaller high frequency credit product, alongside
a digital wallet, UPI payments, and a proprietary alternative- data credit scoring engine.

Truebalance plans to transition toward a broader neo-bank offering by integrating credit, payments,
and, overtime, savings and insurance products. The company also raised debt to expand lending
capacity and support AUM growth. The roadmap also includes diversification beyond personal
loans and increased use of AI-driven underwriting and personalization.

In FY25, net revenue stood at Rs7.8bn, up 34% YoY. Over, FY22-25, revenue grew at a 52% Cagr,
driven by scaling of loan book. PAT rose 31% YoY to 1bn with profitability showing an improving
trend on better operating leverage. PAT has grown at ~220% Cagr over FY22-25.

The company was last valued at Rs15bn (US$168mn) & in its latest funding round in Dec-25, it
raised $75mn in debt by Community Investment Management. Key shareholders include SoftBank
Ventures Asia, Z Venture Capital, Dsaeung Private Equity, and BonAngels Venture Partners.

Fibe (Social Worth Technologies Private Limited)                                                                                          Fibe operates a digital lending platform
                                                                                                                                          focused on unsecured PLs, with FY25 NII of
Fibe, founded in 2015 by Akshay Mehrotra (Group CEO) and Ashish Goyal, is headquartered in
                                                                                                                                          Rs5.4bn
Pune. The company operates a digital lending platform under its consumer-facing brand "Fibe". The
platform follows a hybrid on-book and off-book model, combining balance-sheet lending with co-
lending and service fees from partner banks and NBFCs. Operations are pan-India spanning across
350+ cities.

The company's product portfolio includes unsecured personal loans (majority of the book), short-
term cash loans, BNPL offerings for education, healthcare and consumer durables, loans against
mutual funds, and rooftop solar financing. Revenue is primarily driven by interest income from on-
book assets and fee income from off-book originations.

Fibe's AUM (99% PLs) stood at Rs529bn in FY25 (rising 64% YoY), with c.51-58% on-book and
the balance off-book. GNPA was 3.07% in FY25 (vs. 2.67%, FY24), while NNPA improved to 0.89%
from 1.30%. In FY25, the company launched digital fixed deposits through partner institutions and
expanded into rooftop solar lending, alongside implementation of RBI digital lending guidelines.

The company's revenues rose 49% YoY to Rs12.3bn, growing at a 90% Cagr over FY22-25. PAT
stood at Rs1.1bn in FY25 (vs Rs1bn, FY24), up c.12% YoY. The company has scaled profitability
over the last three years, while profit margins have improved simultaneously. In FY25, Fibe's NIMs
on AUM declined to 17% (vs 18%, FY24) due to a shift towards higher-ticket and longer-tenure
loans. Opex to AUM improved to 8.9% in FY25 (10.6%, FY24), while credit costs (incl FLDG payout)
increased to 11% (8.6%, FY24), leading to RoAUM moderation in FY25. In 1QFY26, total income
stood at Rs3.6bn (vs Rs2.7bn, 1QFY25) and PAT at Rs390mn (Rs250mn, 1QFY25), with RoAUM
improving to 2.9% driven by lower credit costs and opex.

The latest equity round was in Dec-25, where Fibe raised US$35mn at a post-money valuation
of Rs58bn (US$648mn). Founders hold over 10% combined ownership, while major institutional

Refyne Finance Private Limited                                                                                                         RFPL, operational for just over a year, offers
                                                                                                                                       longer-tenure loans for salaried employees in
Refyne Finance (RFPL), an NBFC incorporated in 2021 by Chitresh Sharma (CEO) & Apoorv Kumar
                                                                                                                                       India
(CTO), is based in Bengaluru. The present directors of the company include Chitresh Sharma,
Deepak Mohan Ahuja (CFO), Apoorv Kumar and Naresh Vatwani. RFPL, operational for just over a
year, offers longer-tenure loans for salaried employees in India. The company operates within the
Refyne Holdings Inc. alongside its sister company, Refyne Tech Pvt Ltd (RTPL).

RTPL's flagship product is Salary On-Demand, which lets employees withdraw accrued salary
before payday through integrations with employer HRMS and ERP systems. Revenue of the RTPL
is generated through withdrawal-linked fees and employer-paid software fees. In Mar-26, Acuite
assigned & reaffirmed RFPL's Stable/BBB+ rating across multiple long-term facilities.

The company works with 500+ corporate partners and a cumulative employee base of over 6m, with
some concentration toward a few major clients. As on Dec-25, Refyne's AUM stood at c.Rs10bn.
On standalone financials, total income in FY25 stood at Rs23mn with NII up 72% YoY to Rs11mn
(vs Rs6mn, FY24), while PAT declined 69% YoY to Rs1.2mn in FY25 (vs Rs3.9mn, FY24). As of
9MFY26, its gross income rose to Rs964mn, and PAT stood at Rs140mn. RFPL's net worth rose to
Rs2,424mn (vs Rs960mn, FY25) by Dec-25. The CAR for RFPL stood at 52% as of Mar-25.

In July 2022, during its last funding round, Refyne Finance's parent entity was valued between US
$302-550mn. At the group level, it is backed by Tiger Global, QED Investors, DST Global, RTP Global,
XYZ Venture Capital and Jigsaw. For RFPL itself, both promoters Chitresh Sharma and Apoorv
Kumar hold 37.5% each.

Niyogin was incorporated in 1988 and was acquired and repositioned in 2017 by Information                                              Niyogin operates via Niyogin (NBFC) &
Interface India Private Limited. The company is headquartered in Mumbai and is led by Tashwinder                                       iServeU (Payments infra), with revenues
Singh, Managing Director and CEO. Niyogin Fintech operates through two primary verticals that it                                       driven by payment volumes
aims to demerge into two separate listed entities: a) Niyogin Fintech (Tech-Enabled NBFC) and b)
iServeU (Payments Infrastructure business). Per company, it has received SEBI's approval on the
demerger of the two businesses and awaits the approval from RBI.

The company has a partner-led fintech platform that focuses on MSMEs, offering payments,
lending, and wealth products. Key offerings include a) AePS, DMT, and mATM services via iServeU,
unsecured and secured MSME loans, and b) mutual fund distribution via MoneyFront. Revenue is
primarily driven by payments volumes through iServeU and MSME lending fees, with operations
spanning urban MSMEs and rural retail points across India.

Operationally, AUM stood at Rs3.5bn as of FY26, comprising on-book and off-book MSME loans.
The payments business processed Rs394bn of GTV (incl. payouts) in FY25, reflecting a large rural
footprint, while the company saw a GTV of Rs97bn in 4QFY26. Asset quality improved slightly with
GNPA (net 100% FLDG backed exp.) up 100bps QoQ to 7.9% in 4QFY26.

At the consolidated level, net revenue fell 6% YoY to Rs2.6bn in FY26, however the company
reported a PAT of Rs4mn (vs loss of Rs163mn, FY25), indicating YoY loss narrowing. Revenue grew
at 27% Cagr over FY22-26, while losses narrowed over time due to scale benefits, partially offset
by technology costs, employee expenses, and credit costs.

The company's current market cap is c.Rs5bn (US$56mn). As of Dec-25, promoters held ~40%,
foreign institutional investors (Cohesion MK, Think India Opps, Strategic India Equity Fund among
others) held 20%, and public shareholders held 40%.

Neo Banks                                                                                                                                 Globally, Neo-Banks are often fully licensed
                                                                                                                                          banks that compete with incumbent banks
Neo-Banks have positioned themselves as digital-first banks that operate without traditional brick-
and-mortar branches and focus on digital channels to simplify account financial services. In India,
since RBI doesn’t grant virtual banking licenses, these platforms operate as Fintech wrappers in
partnership with traditional banks. Leading Neo Banks in India include:

•         Jupiter with focus on retail/ personal finance segments & partners with Federal Bank

•         Fi Money that is focused on retail/ salaried professionals and now moving into SME/
          commercial clients and partners with Federal Bank
•         Niyo that focuses on SME and retail customers & partners with SBM Bank & DCB Bank

•         Open that operates in SME/ commercial segment and partners with ICICI Bank

•         FamPay that operates among retail segment and partners with IDFC First Bank

Globally, Neo-Banks are often fully licensed banks that compete with incumbent banks and leverage
on digital offering and wide product suite. The leading Neo-Bank platforms include Nubank (Brazil)
with +100m customers, Revolut (UK) with 65m customers, Monozo (UK) with 14m customers, SoFi
(USA) with 14m customers and Chime (USA) with 25m customers.

In India, the opportunities for Neo-Banks include the ability to leverage low-cost digital platforms to
take financial services to under-banks, hyper-personalization and seamless/quick onboarding. The
challenges arise from high cost of acquisition as well as low monetisation (especially as payments/
UPI is free in India) and lower brand-franchise and direct licensing regime.

Amica Finance has scaled to AUM of Rs.2.5bn as of Dec-2024. Jupiter received final RBI
authorization for Prepaid Payments Instruments issuance in Jun-2024, that can help to lower
dependence on partner banks.

Jupiter has built a user base of 3mn users, primarily salaried millennials across Tier 1 and 2 cities,
with engagement driven by credit usage. The lending book operates at 14-16% net interest margins,
and credit costs stood at 8.8% of disbursements as of Dec-2024, consistent with market standards.
Spend-to-earn improved to 6.45 in FY24, indicating better efficiency as lending income scaled and
customer acquisition costs reduced.

In FY25, revenue stood at Rs564mn, up 57% YoY, and a revenue CAGR of 182% from FY23-25.
Adjusted EBITDA for FY25 was at (Rs.1.9bn), vs (Rs2,5bn) in FY24, margins improved from -27% to
-21% from FY25. Net loss narrowed to (Rs.2.2bn) in FY25, vs (Rs.2.8bn).

Amica was last valued at Rs43bn ($487mn) in a strategic round led by PeakXV Partners and Matrix.
Other key shareholders include Tiger Global, Nubank, Beenext, QED Investors.

Open Money (Open Financial Technologies Pvt. Ltd.)                                                                                       Open Money offers an integrated banking
                                                                                                                                         platform for SMEs, combining banking,
Open Money, founded in May 2017 by Anish Achuthan (CEO), Mabel Chacko, Deena Jacob,
                                                                                                                                         accounting, and expense mgt
and Ajeesh Achuthan and headquartered in Bengaluru, operates a connected banking platform
that unifies banking, accounting, and expense management for SMEs. Its business spans three
verticals: a) Open Money (SME neo-banking), b) Zwitch (embedded finance), and c) BankingStack
(enterprise SaaS), with revenue driven by subscriptions, transaction fees, and enterprise contracts.
In Dec 2023, the company secured an RBI Payment Aggregator license, enabling direct merchant
settlement and margin improvement. The platform serves over 3.5mn businesses.

In FY25, revenue rose 85% YoY to Rs460mn, recovering from prior-year contraction and delivering a
24% CAGR over FY22-25. Adjusted EBITDA losses reduced from Rs2bn in FY22 to Rs0.6bn in FY25,
reflecting expense rationalization and progress towards unit economics. Net losses narrowed in
FY25 to Rs1bn from Rs1.7bn, FY24.

The company was valued at Rs73bn ($940mn) in a Series D round led by IIFL Finance in May 2022.
Shareholding includes founders at 26% and institutional investors at 63%, with key backers such
as Temasek Holdings and Tiger Global.

Insurtech                                                                                                                            ~4% of India's insurance premiums are
                                                                                                                                     sourced digitally in FY25, with higher
India's InsurTech space has also emerged into a diversified segment that comprises: (1) digital
                                                                                                                                     penetration in term & health insurance
only distributors, (2) POSP distribution models, (3) digital first manufacturers, and (4) value chain
innovators such as administration and risk management platforms. In India, only c.4% of overall
insurance premiums are mobilised digitally with penetration being higher in term insurance and
health insurance segments, followed by motor insurance and savings linked life insurance plans.
Despite the low penetration insurtech revenues have grown strongly with scale up distribution
platforms and manufacturers. We expect the segment to see 27% Cagr in premium mobilisation
over next five years.

We profile four InsurTech companies in this segment with aggregate revenues of c.Rs85bn and
market valuation (based on market cap and last deal) of US$12bn. Among these companies, PB
Fintech (Policy Bazaar) has emerged as the market leader in online distribution of insurance policies
(and loans) and also delivered impressive improvement in profitability, which is evident from stock
returns over past three years. Among the digital first insurance manufacturers, Acko has developed
a digital-first insurance platform led by motor segment and over past three years has grown overall
premiums at 28% Cagr (without adjusting for impact of 1/n rule on accounting). Some players have
also ramped up in the POSP segment for distribution of policies, however we understand that net
take-rates are lower in this segment.

PolicyBazaar, founded by Yashish Dahiya, Alok Bansal, and Avaneesh Nirjar is headquartered in                                  PB Fintech expanded beyond online
Gurugram. It operates as a digital distribution platform for insurance and credit products through                             insurance into lending product distribution,
its flagship brands PolicyBazaar and Paisabazaar. The company earns revenue from insurance                                     offline & commercial insurance
commissions, renewal fees, and credit disbursals, targeting the Indian mass market and NRIs. It is
led by Group CEO Yashish Dahiya.

PB Fintech has expanded beyond the core online insurance selling platform into distribution of
lending products, offline insurance sales through own & POSP channels, commercial insurance.
The new initiatives account for 40% of the total company revenues, with expansion supported by
PB Fintech's balance sheet. It has also built presence in the UAE and has also announced plans to
make some investment in healthcare segment.

Financially, FY25 operating revenue stood at Rs50bn, up 45% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of
Rs940mn (1.9% margin) and PAT of Rs3.5bn. Revenue grew at a CAGR of 40% over FY23-25 as the
business transitioned from historical losses to profitability, supported by expanding EBITDA and
PAT margins.

The company raised Rs56bn at a valuation of $6bn during its IPO in November 2021. As of Jul-26,
the market cap stood at Rs776bn ($8.4bn)The shareholding structure is led by Foreign Institutions
(48%) & Corporate Bodies such as Info Edge (13%), and Domestic Institutions (18%).

Acko Technology & Services Private Limited                                                            Acko operates as the only full-stack D2C
                                                                                                      insurance platform, with FY25 premiums at
Acko, founded by Varun Dua and Ruchi Deepak and headquartered in Bengaluru, operates as
                                                                                                      Rs28bn (up 35% YoY)
the only full-stack Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) insurance platform underwriting motor, retail health,
corporate group health, and life insurance products. Motor insurance remains the key category
for Acko, where the company has differentiated by building its network of franchise garages. This
improves services (customers get free road-side assistance) and claim costs are also controlled.
Interestingly, both life and general insurance subsidiaries sit below the Hold Co.

Recent developments include entry into life insurance with the Acko Flexi Term Plan, acquisition of
chronic care management firm OneCare, and the resignation of the general insurance entity’s MD
& CEO Sanjeev Srinivasan. Operational highlights feature a Claim Settlement Ratio of 99.9% and
reduced marketing dependence, reflected in an 12% YoY drop in ad spend in FY25.

Acko Insurance compares with Progressive and GEICO, which are established U.S. giants. The
extensive use of tech platforms and D2C approach among insurers helps them to offer better
prices, customise products/ offers to customers' behaviour and requirements. The global players
are focussed on segments like motor, home and besides other segments.

In FY26, GWP stood at Rs27bn, up 32% YoY (10%, FY25), with mix for health increasing to 51% &
Motor at 43%. The company's Loss Ratio continued to improve & stood at 66% in FY26 (70%,FY25),
with combined ratio and underwriting losses narrowing to 10% and Rs2bn. GWP grew at a Cagr of
22% over FY23-26, with losses reducing due to operating leverage & cost controls.

InsuranceDekho (Girnar Insurance Brokers Private Limited)                                                      In Nov-25, InsuranceDekho received CCI
                                                                                                               approval for a share-swap merger with
InsuranceDekho, founded by Ankit Agrawal (CEO) and Ish Babbar and headquartered in Gurugram,
                                                                                                               RenewBuy
operates a B2B2C insurtech model built on the Point of Sale Person (POSP) framework. The
company focuses on assisted insurance distribution across Tier 2, Tier 3, and rural India, offering
motor, health, life, and SME insurance products. It runs a phygital model combining a large on-
ground agent network with a digital policy issuance and claims platform. Premium mix has been
consistently shifting towards non-motor categories like health, life & commercial lines (the last one
being unique to them), while the mix of PSU players has been rising in overall premiums. On the

GST waiver w.e.f. Sep-25, the company indicated that the reform led to sum insured increasing by
20-25% vs earlier, aiding higher value growth, over and above the uptick already seen in volumes.

In November 2025, the CCI approved a share-swap merger with RenewBuy, creating a scaled
challenger in insurance distribution. The combined entity manages a network of over 220,000
POSPs and covers 99% of Indian pin codes, with Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities accounting for 86% of
its agent base. The platform distributes over 380 insurance products sourced from more than 46
insurance partners, with insurance brokerage as the primary revenue driver. Effectively, their merger
should help increase geographical presence given it is South & East focused, while ID is more North
& West focused.

Financially, FY25 revenue rose to Rs13bn, up 74% YoY, and grown from Rs0.5bn in FY22. Adj.
EBITDA loss (excluding ESOP) level declined to Rs316mn in FY25 with a margin of -2% (vs 10%,
FY24), driven by merger integration and cost controls. In FY25 it reported a loss of Rs474m (vs
profit of Rs857mn, FY24), while it recorded profits on Ebitda level in Sep-25. The POSP channel has
better loss as well as opex ratios vs traditional channels like agency. For instance, it's usually 30%
opex ratio for tech-enabled distributors vs 38-40% for agencies.

The company was valued at Rs65bn when it raised Rs700mn in a Series C round in Mar-25 led
by Beams Fintech, with participation from MUFG and BNP Paribas. The cap table includes Girnar
Software and Amit Jain holding over 50%, while TVS Capital, Goldman Sachs, MUFG, and BNP
Paribas together hold 31%.

RenewBuy, founded by Balachander Sekhar (CEO) and Indraneel Chatterjee is headquartered
in Gurugram. It operates a B2B2C digital agent network model offering motor, health, and life
insurance products. Commissions from insurance carriers remain the primary revenue driver. The
platform has a wide geographic reach across 1,500 towns and partners with over 35 insurance
companies.

Operating metrics show 125,000 insurance advisors and 2.5mn customers insured as of 2022.
70% of its revenue comes from outside the top 30 cities, with a strong focus on semi-urban and
rural markets. RenewBuy's revenues grew at a CAGR of 130% over FY22-24. In FY24, it recorded
a revenue of Rs4bn (175% YoY) and adj. EBITDA loss stood at Rs635mn. Net losses widened to
Rs650mn in FY24 (vs Rs746mn, FY23).

WealthTech: Expanding wallet share to grow revenues                                                                                   Groww is the largest broker w.r.t. active
                                                                                                                                      clients, while Zerodha has the highest
Wealth and investment management is a Rs1tn market (in revenue terms) in India primarily
                                                                                                                                      revenue amongst brokers
comprising brokers and traditional wealth managers. This market is expected to grow at 15-17%
Cagr over the next five years with wealth & asset management growing faster at ~20%. The
broking business has witnessed emergence of digital only players post COVID driven by flat pricing,
faster onboarding and growing share of investors below 30 years. In contrast, wealth management
business has been dominated by traditional players with relationship manager led models. This
could be changing with emergence of tech led peers such as Dezerv, and brokers like GROWW (W
for Wealth) and Angel One (IONIQ Wealth) expanding into the space.

While GROWW is the largest broker w.r.t. active clients, Zerodha has the highest revenue amongst
brokers. Profitability of digital brokers such as GROWW, Zerodha, Angel One has grown >3x over the
last five years driven by increasing market share, and expanding retail participation in equities and
options. However, FY25 was a year of moderation with revenue momentum slowing as regulations
limited the weekly option market and cash market volumes also fell. This has resulted in brokers
expanding services to wealth management and lending.

We profile eight online broking and wealth management companies in this segment with aggregate
revenues of c.Rs226bn in FY25 and market valuation (based on market cap and last deal) of
US$32bn. We think growth from here will be a function of diversification (e.g. MTF, wealth
management, insurance distribution), mining of existing assets on the platform and new product
launches.

Groww (Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd)                                                                                           As 45% of Groww's clients are below the
                                                                                                                                    age of 30 years, client assets can grow with
Groww, founded in 2016 by Lalit Keshre, Harsh Jain, Neeraj Singh, and Ishan Bansal is
                                                                                                                                    vintage
headquartered in Bengaluru. Groww is the largest broker in India w.r.t. active clients, noting its +26%
market share (2nd has 16% market share). As 45% of Groww's clients are below the age of 30 years,
client assets can grow with vintage. Further, clients who have been on the platform for 3-4 years
have 4-5x the assets they started with.

During FY25, Groww reported revenues of Rs39bn and has grown at 85% CAGR over FY23-25. It
reported adjusted Ebitda of Rs21bn, implying margin of 55%, and profit of Rs18bn.

Groww is following a model similar to Robinhood with its launch of margin trading facility (MTF),
expansion into new asset classes (e.g. commodities & bonds), launch of new products (e.g., wealth
management & loans against securities) & product innovations (915 platform for active traders). We
estimate these business could contribute Rs17bn in revenues by FY28e (23% of FY28e revenues)
& 30% of FY28e adj. EBITDA, with MTF & wealth being the key contributors.

As of Jul-26, the market cap is Rs1,287bn (US$14bn). 27% is owned by promoters, FIIs own 3%,
DIIs own 6%, and retail investors own 64%.

Zerodha Broking Limited                                                                                                               Zerodha's revenue is primarily driven by
                                                                                                                                      F&O volumes, with diversification into AMC,
Zerodha, founded in 2010 by Nithin Kamath (CEO) and Nikhil Kamath is headquartered in Bengaluru.
                                                                                                                                      lending, insurance
The company operates a discount brokerage model offering equity, currency, and commodity
trading via its Kite platform, alongside mutual fund investments through Coin and investor
education via Varsity. Revenue is primarily driven by Futures & Options (F&O) volumes, while
diversification includes asset management through Zerodha Fund House, lending via Zerodha
Capital, and insurance through Ditto, with plans to enable US stock investing via GIFT City.

Recent regulatory changes include SEBI’s Oct 2024 overhaul of index derivatives, which resulted
in 12%/23% revenue/PAT contraction in FY25 (Nov'25, Entracker) and 40% decline in 1QFY26
revenues (30 Sep 25; Times of India). Meanwhile, Zerodha Fund House surpassed Rs100bn in AUM.
As on FY25, the firm serves 7.5mn active clients, holding a ~16% market share on NSE.

In FY25, revenue declined 11% YoY to Rs88bn, while adjusted EBITDA (pre-ESOP) fell 19% to
Rs56bn, and net profit dropped 23% YoY to Rs42bn, impacted by lower topline. In FY24, revenue was
Rs100bn, adjusted EBITDA Rs70bn (70% margin), and net profit Rs55bn. Over FY22-25, revenue
grew at a 21% CAGR, and EBITDA more than doubled, reflecting strong historical growth despite
recent headwinds.

The company is bootstrapped, with an est. valuation of Rs871bn ($10.5bn) as of Apr-25.

Upstox (RKSV Securities India Private Limited)                                                                                        Upstox’s earns via brokerage, interest
                                                                                                                                      income, & trx charges, with a user base
Upstox, founded by Ravi Kumar (CEO), Raghu Kumar, Shrinivas Viswanath, and Kavitha
                                                                                                                                      concentrated in Tier-2/3 cities
Subramanian is headquartered in India. The company operates a digital-first discount brokerage
platform offering equity delivery, intraday trading, F&O trading, margin trading, and allied wealth
products. Revenue is primarily driven by brokerage fees, interest income, and transaction-related
charges, with a pan-India presence concentrated in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities. Upstox has lost active
clients and market share and its active client base has declined from 5.2m in Mar-22 to 2.7m in
Mar-25.

It 17mn registered users, with 85% users from non-metro regions. In FY25, revenue saw a slight
decline of 1% YoY to Rs9.5bn, while adjusted Ebitda (ex-ESOP) decreased to Rs242mn. Adj Ebitda
margins contracted to 3% (vs 8%, FY25) on higher expenses. PAT rose 22% YoY to Rs2bn on back
of higher other income. Upstox delivered a 7% revenue Cagr over FY22-25, and its profitability
improved significantly as adjusted Ebitda/PAT shifted from a Rs6bn/Rs7bn loss in FY22 to a
positive Rs242mn/Rs2bn in FY25, respectively.

The latest disclosed valuation was Rs238bn (US$3bn). In Nov-21, the company held a Series C
round led by Tiger Global. Shareholding is led by Tiger Global as the largest institutional investor,
with founding promoters holding ~36% on a consolidated basis.

AngelOne                                                                                                                         AngelOne has +2.3mn SIPs registered
                                                                                                                                 clients, Rs167bn     MF AUM,  credit
AngelOne was founded by Dinesh Thakkar (CEO) in 1996, and is headquartered in Mumbai,
                                                                                                                                 disbursements at Rs27bn
India. The company operates as a full service digital brokerage platform offering equity broking,
derivatives, commodities, currency trading, mutual funds, IPO distribution, margin funding, and
advisory services. Revenue is primarily driven by brokerage, interest income, distributional income
from financials products, fess from wealth and asset management. The company has been
diversifying into life insurance through a JV with LivWell, committing Rs4bn to build a digital-first,
pure protection insurance business. It has 2.3 mn+ SIPs registered clients, Rs167bn in mutual fund
AUM, credit disbursements have reached Rs27bn. Wealth Management AUM was at Rs101bn and
asset management AUM stood at Rs4bn, aided by passive funds.

Angel One has c.7mn clients as of Mar-26 with 18%/ 22% market share in cash and F&O ADTO. It has
accelerated its shift from a broking-led model to a full-stack fintech platform. In FY26, revenues fell
2% YoY to Rs51bn, while adjusted Ebitda (ex-ESOP) was down 4% to Rs20bn. Margins on adj Ebitda
level were only slightly down at 39%. However, Ebitda margins fell 3ppt YoY to 35% in FY26 due to
higher opex & softer top-line growth. With rising cost of acquisition, margins fell over FY23-26, with
Adj Ebitda margins down from 45% in FY23. PAT declined 22% YoY to Rs9bn. It delivered a 20%
revenue Cagr over FY23-26, with profitability improving at a slower pace over the same period.

As of Jan-2026, the market cap is Rs311bn ($3.3bn). 29% is owned by promoters, FIIs own 13%,
DIIs own 15%, and retail investors own 43%.

Trader App, Dhan Web, ScanX, and deep integration with TradingView to support advanced trading
workflows.

Dhan’s revenue is primarily generated from brokerage fees and commissions (88% of revenues in
FY25), interest income from its Margin Trading Facility, and subscription fees from the DhanHQ

Fyers Securities Private Limited (Fyers)

Fyers was founded in 2015 by Tejas Khoday (CEO), Yashas Khoday and Shreyas Khoday and is
headquartered in Bengaluru, India. The company operates a digital stockbroking and wealth-tech
platform focused on active traders and high-frequency users. Product offerings include equity
broking, derivatives and commodities trading, mutual fund distribution, API-based algorithmic
trading, Margin Trading Facility (MTF), and trading automation tools such as FYERS Web, FYERS
App, FYERS Direct and FYERS Automate. Operations are pan-India with a recent extension to NRI
clients.

Fyers follows a hybrid business model with revenues generated from broking fees and non-broking
income. In FY24, broking contributed ~50% of revenue, while non-broking income including MTF
contributed ~50%, with management indicating a shift toward a higher MTF share. As of FY25,
total customers exceeded 750,000, with ~225,811 active NSE clients. The MTF loan book was est.
at Rs3-4bn in FY24, with interest rates ranging from 12.5%-16.5%. The company expanded MTF
limits from Rs2.5mn to Rs5mn per client and initiated a Rs2bn commercial paper program to fund
loan book growth. Headcount increased to ~390-395 employees in FY25. Recent developments
include the application for SEBI approval for a Rs10bn Category-III AIF, which is intended to diversify
revenue toward asset management, separate from the core broking and MTF businesses.

FY25 revenue was Rs2.7bn, up ~5% YoY, with adjusted Ebitda of Rs306mn on a 11% margin. PAT
stood at Rs526mn in FY25, growing at 33% Cagr over FY22-25. Revenues grew at a 40% Cagr over
FY22-25, but adj. Ebitda margins have declined in FY25 from 22% in FY22. Slight improvement in
profitability over the years was driven by higher trading activity and increasing contribution from
MTF income, while no material credit costs were reported due to the fully collateralised nature of
lending.

Jar (ChangeJar Technologies Private Limited)                                                                                   Jar is a micro-saving platform in the form of
                                                                                                                               gold that is stored in third-party vaults
Jar, founded in Jan 2021 by Nishchay AG (CEO) and Misbah Ashraf is headquartered in Bengaluru.
The company operates a wealth-tech platform offering automated digital gold accumulation, D2C
jewelry under the brand Nek, and credit distribution, generating revenue through gold spreads,
jewelry margins, and loan origination fees. Its user base is concentrated in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.

In response to claims that Jar may have collected money from the public through a digital gold
savings scheme without regulatory approval, Jar has clarified that it is a micro-saving platform, and
that its gold is securely stored in third-party vaults.

In Oct-24, the company launched Nek and achieved cash flow profitability in 2HFY25. The platform
has a user base of 20mn+. The company has also leveraged its growing scale to directly source gold
and manage inventory risks that aid better margins. The ability to protect daily investment limits is
higher as investors commit to daily investment plans that may gold purchases along predictable
lines.

In FY25, operating revenue surged to Rs24.5bn, up from Rs490mn in FY24, growing 49x YoY, due
to a shift to a principal-based revenue recognition model reflecting shift in business model to self
sourcing of gold. Net losses narrowed in FY25 to Rs0.5bn (vs Rs1bn, FY24). It has turned profitable
since Jan-25 and recorded an unaudited revenue of Rs86bn with operation revenue of Rs5.5bn.

Jar's last disclosed valuation was Rs19bn ($0.2bn) during a fundraise in Aug-22. Shareholding
includes founders at 45%, institutional investors such as Tiger Global, Arkam Ventures other
investors at 45%, and an ESOP pool of 10%.

SaaS & Others                                                                                                                     SaaS platforms offer cloud-native, API-first
                                                                                                                                  tools, helping banks/ fintechs to scale digital
Fintech SaaS (Software-as-a-Service) platforms provide cloud-native, API-first solutions that enable
                                                                                                                                  financial products
banks, fintechs, and enterprises to build, manage, and scale digital financial products. Their focus
spans digital payments, core banking, lending, credit issuance, and embedded finance. Over the
past few years, these companies have expanded outside Indian client base as well. These platforms
target legacy banking inefficiencies, providing modular, high-speed, and customizable technology
stacks. Some of the key SAAS plays in India are Perfios, Yubi, Zeta, Account Aggregators (for lenders
and wealth management platforms), and M2P Solutions among others. We have profiled some of
the leading ones here along with growth and profitability trends.

Account Aggregator: Digitising data flow for lenders & non-lending                                                                While there are 17 NBFC-AAs, the top 6
financials                                                                                                                        players would have 98-99% market share
In 2016, RBI authorised a new segment of services provides, Account Aggregators (AA) to operate
through a specified NBFC license- NBFC-AA. The object was to facilitate lending through collection
of financial asset and income data of potential borrowers and share with prospective lenders.
In order to prevent data-leakage, NBFC-AA weren't allowed to see the data (so they were data-
blind) and borrowers' specific permission was mandated. They procure data of customers from
Financial Information Providers (FIPs) and share with Financial Information Users (FIUs). While RBI
is the regulator, there is expectation that industry body Sahmati will be appointed as Self Regulator
Organisation (SRO) for the sector.

Currently, there are 17 AA that are licensed in India and since their formation they have served
150-200m unique users, completing 80-90m cumulative consents per month. Major consumers of
the requests are lenders (NBFCs and bank), wealthtech & broking platforms as well as insurers. In
the lending segment, the usage is higher for consumer durable loans, unsecured personal loans but

relatively lower for home loans or vehicle loans where lenders have reasonable information about
borrowers.

Today, roughly 10% of system-wide loans use AA rails, and we understand the industry expects
penetration to rise to 30-40% as joint and corporate account data becomes permitted and
underwriting adoption increases. Lending remains underwriting-led and mostly one-off, while new
use cases such as loan monitoring, loan collections, and recurring analytics-driven fetches are
gaining traction. Fair-use rules introduced in the past year have also helped reduce unnecessary
request volumes and increased comfort among banks.

One of the key reasons why the adoption hasn't risen sharply is the limitation of data that AA
can access and share with users. AAs can procure banking information from single savings and
current accounts, but can't access joint bank accounts or fixed deposits, which is an important
form of deposits people keep, especially self-employed people. Additional data sources such as
GST and LAS data are available but see uneven adoption due to coverage and attribute-quality gaps.
Pricing compression is ongoing due to limited differentiation in the core utility offering, and market
participants are exploring standardization of utility-cost structures. One area where regulator has
helped to remove hurdles is around streamlining. The rules for 'Fair Use' of data and the participants
can set limitations on generating unused requests. This has comforted FIPs to open data with AAs
and FIUs.

While there are 17 NBFC-AAs, the top 6 players would have 98-99% market share with platforms
like Cookiejar, One Money, Anumati, CAMS and NADL being the leading ones. Monetisation
opportunity has lagged expectations due to slower adoption and compression in pricing. AAs are
also leveraging on TSP business to provide data analytic services to

Perfios, founded in 2008 by V.R. Govindarajan and Debasish Chakraborty and headquartered in

Mumbai, is led by Sabyasachi Goswami (CEO). Perfios positions itself as a foundational digital

infrastructure provider for the BFSI ecosystem, with deep domain expertise built over the years. The
company operates as a B2B Fintech provider for the BFSI sector, focusing on the lending lifecycle
through a) onboarding, b) data-driven decision-making and analytics, and c) monitoring products.
Key offerings include Bank Statement Analyzer, Karza Technologies identity verification, and the
Anumati Account Aggregator.

Perfios operates across 18 countries and the maturity levels vary by market: some geographies
are well established, others are still in early penetration stages. International operations (built over
six years) follow the same Indian product lines but require much deeper regulatory compliance.
Presently, its revenue is entirely service-based, with India contributing c.90% of the total revenues
and international markets at 10%.

It has recently launched 'Journey Builder', an AI-Powered low-code platform for financial institutions
to design, launch, and optimise product journeys. Reduces turnaround development time of new
journeys by over 60%. It can gather customer behavioural and other data patterns from both
internal and external sources and convert these into corresponding end to end journeys. Key
Features and Benefits of Perfios Journey Builder include (1) Visual Journey Composition for drag-
and-drop workflow builder, (2) Modular & Reusable Components, (3) Pre-Integrated Ecosystem
with connectors for digitisation, document classification, credit bureaus, KYC, and fraud checks,
streamlining complex workflows, (4) Journey-Native Analytics besides other features.

The company wants to operate only in geographies and segments where it can be the clear category
leader, avoiding resource dilution in opportunistic or non-scalable markets. Over the next 2-5 years,
the focus will be on creating category-defining products rather than chasing incremental features.

In FY25, revenue grew 20% YoY to Rs6.7bn, while adjusted Ebitda (pre-ESOP) reached Rs1.8bn on a
27% margin (+6pp YoY, vs 21% in FY24). PAT surged 46% YoY to Rs1bn in FY25 with PAT margins
improving 3pp YoY to 16% (vs 13%, FY24). Revenue expanded from Rs1.4bn in FY22, delivering a
CAGR of 70% over FY22-25. Adj. Ebitda margins have risen steadily on the back of improved unit
economics, while profitability has strengthened consistently over FY22-25.

Perfios was valued at Rs101bn ($1.2bn) in May-25 following a $80mn Series D round in Mar 2024
led by Teachers’ Venture Growth and Kedaara Capital. Shareholding includes institutional investors
at 78%, founders at 9%, and an ESOP pool of 8%, with investors such as Warburg Pincus, Kedaara
Capital, and Bessemer Venture Partners.

Zeta is a banking-tech infrastructure company founded in 2015 by Bhavin Turakhia (CEO) and
Ramki Gaddipati. It operates through a multi-entity structure, with the US serving as the commercial

headquarters, India functioning as the primary R&D centre under Better World Technology Pvt                                            Zeta's revenue model is built on long-term
Ltd and Singapore managing Asian and MENA operations. The company provides a cloud-native,                                             SaaS contracts, licensing fees & usage-
API-first banking stack called Tachyon, and its product offerings include a) core banking ledger                                       based trx pricing
functions, b) issuer processing for credit/debit products, and d) digital issuance tools like digital
credit as a service for credit line on UPI (CLOU). Its revenue model is built on long-term SaaS
contracts, licensing fees and usage-based transaction pricing.

The company's customer base is concentrated in India due to the scale of deployments with
HDFC Bank. It also enabled HDFC Bank’s Pixel credit card, launched in 2024, and rebuilt the bank’s
PayZapp app, which has now onboarded more than 7mn users. Zeta has also invested in building
a dedicated Digital Credit-as-a-Service platform for the Credit Line on UPI framework, following
regulatory approval of credit-line-linking on UPI rails. Operationally, Zeta has more than 1,700
employees globally, with over 70% in tech and product roles. The company processes more than
25mn live accounts on its platform and has a similar volume of contracted accounts in migration. Its
global burn rate has been reduced to ~$22mn per year in 2024 from a historical peak of $60-70mn.

Financially, the India entity reported Rs6bn revenue in FY25, down 33% YoY. Its Ebitda stood at
Rs772mn with margins contracting by 4pp YoY to 13% in FY25. PAT was down c.55% YoY to
Rs535mn in FY25 on revenue decline and PAT margins fell 4pp YoY to 9% in FY25. Revenue grew
from Rs3bn in FY21 to Rs6bn in FY25, implying a 19% Cagr over FY21-25. Profitability was primarily
affected by employee-related costs that were 76% of the FY25 revenues (vs 69% in FY24).

Zeta’s latest valuation stands at Rs174bn ($2bn) post-money, following the $50mn Series D round
in Feb-2025 led by Optum. Prior investors include SoftBank, Pluxee and Mastercard. The founders
collectively hold an ~60-65% stake, SoftBank Vision c.15-17%, Sodexo at c.10%, ESOP pool at
c.5-7%, Mastercard at c.2%, while Optum’s Series D investment translates to c.2.5% ownership.

Yubi (CredAvenue Private Limited)

Yubi, founded in Aug 2020 by CEO Gaurav Kumar and Vineet Sukumar as a spin-off from Vivriti
Capital and headquartered in Chennai. It runs five core platforms: Yubi Loans, Yubi Co.Lend,
Aspero, Yubi Flow, and Spocto, with revenue driven by transaction fees, platform subscriptions, and
collection services.

The platform integrates 6,200+ investors and lenders with 17,000+ enterprise partners and
processed Rs1.4tn in total debt volumes in FY25, including Rs469bn in Direct Assignments
and Rs53bn in Pass-Through Certificates. It handles 20mn+ transactions annually, averaging
80,000 daily loan transactions, with 79% of loans reaching Tier-2/3 cities, indicating deep market
penetration. Recently, it expanded into the MENA region via Yubi One and partnered with SBI to
digitize co-lending. Co-lending disbursements have exceeded Rs100bn.

In FY25, revenue increased 36% YoY to Rs6.6bn, and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs1.3bn,
though net losses rose slightly to Rs4.2bn due to continued tech investments. Revenue has grown
at a 59% CAGR over FY22-25, while EBITDA margins improved from -145% in FY23 to -38% in FY25.

Yubi raised Rs4bn in late 2025 and is currently valued at Rs107bn ($1.2bn). Shareholding includes
Vivriti Capital at 50%, institutional investors such as Insight Partners and B Capital at 28%, and
founders at 14-15%.

Credgenics (Analog Legalhub Technology Solutions Pvt Ltd)

Credgenics, incorporated in October 2018 & headquartered in Noida, was founded by Rishabh
Goel (CEO), Anand Agrawal and Mayank Khera. The company operates an off-balance-sheet SaaS
platform for debt collections and resolution for banks, NBFCs, HFCs, fintech lenders and ARCs.
Its products include AI-based collections tools, GenAI voice and video solutions, legal recovery
tools, and payments platform to facilitate loan repayments (Billzy). The company earns mainly from
SaaS through subscription fees and usage-based charges for communications and APIs, with 62%
revenue coming from software solutions and the rest from tech-enabled services. It primarily serves
retail and SME/MSME portfolios in India, while expanding into South East Asia and the Middle East.
It managed more than US$250bn of loan accounts on-platform in FY24.

Its recent acquisition of Arrise in Aug-25 added 5k+ professionals across 18k+ pin codes and
25+ states in its field collections network. In Mar-2026, Credgenics also expanded into insurance
through CredInsure, a platform for renewals, premium collections, onboarding, servicing, upsell,
cross-sell and lapse recovery. The company served 160+ financial institutions as on FY25,
handled 98mn+ retail loan accounts worth US$250bn+, and facilitated 1.7bn+ omnichannel
communications. The client base was over 160 by FY25, and employee count stood at 491.

The company’s revenue rose 40% YoY to Rs1.9bn in FY25, implying a 90% Cagr over FY22-25.
FY25 was its first EBITDA-positive year, with adj. Ebitda of Rs130mn (vs. loss of Rs73mn in FY24),
translating into a 7% margin, driven by operating leverage. The company had turned PAT-positive
in FY24, supported by higher other income, and profit increased a further 189% YoY in FY25 to
Rs272mn (vs. Rs94mn in FY24). After losses widened in FY23, the company returned to profitability
in FY24 and saw further earnings expansion in FY25 as revenue growth outpaced operating cost
growth and other income continued to rise.

The latest funding round in Aug-23 valued the company at a Rs28bn (US$340mn) post-money
valuation, led by WestBridge Capital and Accel, with participation from Tanglin Ventures, Beams

is headquartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. The company operates as an off-balance-sheet, asset-

light digital marketplace for retail financial products (it carries no credit risk and earns revenue
entirely through commissions and fees). Its two core revenue drivers are: a) origination fees from
partner banks & NBFCs for loans and credit card issuances, and b) recurring transaction-based fees
and performance incentives from co-branded credit card partnerships (84% of FY25 revenues). Key
product offerings include a) Co-branded credit cards, b) Free credit health monitoring via Experian,
c) Retail lending marketplace spanning personal, home, auto, & education loans, d) Digital gold
loans (via Muthoot Fincorp), and e) Insurance & Investment distribution. India is the primary market,
with offices in Chennai, Bengaluru, and Mumbai.

In early 2025, BankBazaar partnered with Muthoot Fincorp to distribute digital gold loans. Its
platform had +60mn registered users in FY25 (vs 50mn, FY23). Recurring revenue on co-branded
cards was Rs2bn in FY25, a 121% CAGR over FY23-25, with cards-in-force growing 35% YoY in FY25
(vs 62.5%, FY24). The company's headcount declined 17% YoY to 765, reflecting cost rationalisation
and increased automation.

In FY25, revenues grew 33% YoY to Rs2.5bn, while they delivered a 37% Cagr over FY22-25. FY25
revenue grew 33% YoY (vs 18% YoY, FY24). Co-branded card recurring revenue alone was Rs2bn
in FY25, comprising ~84% of total revenues. Adj. Ebitda (ex-Esops) turned positive in FY25 at
Rs40mn (adj. EBITDA margin: ~1%), vs. negative in FY24. Statutory Ebitda margin was -4.4% in
FY25. Net losses narrowed to Rs230mn in FY25 (Rs265mn loss in FY24), driven by improved
operating efficiency. This was led by staff cost optimisation, while ad-spend remained flat across
FY24-25 despite 33% revenue growth. Partially offsetting this, other operating costs rose in FY25 on
platform scaling, and finance costs rose on venture debt servicing. Cash & equivalents on balance
sheet was c.Rs110mn as of FY25.

The company raised Rs41mn in Feb-26 at a post-money valuation of Rs19bn (US$207mn). This
funding round was led by Walden International. Total equity raised since inception stands at ~US
$133-134mn across 11 rounds. The cap table is dominated by institutional investors at ~71%
(Amazon, Peak XV Partners, Walden International, Experian, Fidelity Growth Partners, Eight Roads,
and GUS Holdings), followed by the ESOP pool at c.23%, founders (Adhil Shetty, Arjun Shetty, Rati
Shetty) at ~3.3%, and Muthoot Fincorp at c.1%.

Onemoney (Finsec AA Solutions Private Limited)                                                                                      Onemoney's enables encrypted financial
                                                                                                                                    data transfer between FIPs & FIUs via mobile
Onemoney, founded in 2016 by CEO Krishna Prasad and headquartered in Hyderabad, operates
                                                                                                                                    and web interfaces
as an RBI-licensed Account Aggregator, functioning as a data-blind consent manager that
enables encrypted financial data transfer between Financial Information Providers and Financial
Information Users via mobile and web interfaces. Revenue is generated through transaction
fees for consent processing and bundled solutions supporting lending, underwriting and wealth
management use cases.

In Aug 2024, the company secured an investment from identity platform Equal to offer unified
identity and financial data services, following the exit of earlier investor KFin Technologies. It
processes over 55mn monthly transactions in combination with Equal, holds an estimated 45%
market share, and reports a 97% success rate.

In FY25, revenue continued to grow and stood at Rs102mn (+150% YoY) on back of RBI's structural
push toward the Account Aggregator framework. As major digital lenders and banks transitioned
entirely to cash flow based underwriting, the volumes of consent based data transactions routed
through Onemoney rose exponentially. The company has turned profitable in FY25 with company's
adj Ebitda at Rs25mn (vs loss of Rs66mn in FY24) and PAT at Rs120mn (vs loss of Rs83mn).
Revenue expanded at c.400% Cagr over FY22-25, while adj. Ebitda margins improved to 10% in
FY25 from -350% in FY22, reflecting continued investment in platform capacity and compliance.

As of mid-2025, the company was valued at Rs453mn ($5mn) following Equal’s entry. Shareholding
pattern includes Krishna Prasad & family at 68% and Equal at 26%.

Finvu (Cookiejar Technologies Private Limited)                                                                                             Finvu earns revenue from a) data fetches, b)
                                                                                                                                           consent processing, and c) enterprise usage
Finvu, founded in 2016 by Manoj Alandkar and Munish Bhatia, is headquartered in Pune. It is an
RBI-licensed NBFC Account Aggregator (AA) operating within India’s consent-based financial-data-
sharing framework. The company enables data flows between Financial Information Providers and
Financial Information Users across bank accounts, GST data and securities information. Finvu’s
business is India-focused and built on a utility-style model where revenue comes from a) data
fetches, b) consents processed and c) enterprise usage across lenders, wealth managers, brokers

and analytics firms. Revenue is generated through transaction-based data fetch fees and SaaS
fees for API licensing and analytics. Lending use cases drive the highest activity, mainly consumer
durable loans and unsecured personal loans where the ticket size has increased from Rs60-65k
to Rs80-90k over the past year. NBFCs form the largest share of users, accounting for 95% of
consents, with the top 50 entities contributing roughly 90% of all usage. Our discussions highlight
that monthly volumes include 350-400mn data fetches, of which 30% relate to lending and 70%
to non-lending functions (analytics & nightly refreshes). Monthly consents stand at 80-90mn (3mn
per day), with 70% used in lending and 25% by non-lenders like brokers and wealth managers.
Cumulative unique users are 150-200mn, with 8-10mn unique users each month.

In FY25, revenue rose 40% YoY to Rs105mn, up from Rs75mn in FY24, delivering a 490% Cagr over
FY22-25. Ebitda margins contracted to 27% in FY25 (vs 59%, FY24) on higher employee, advertising
and infrastructure expenses. Net profits were flat YoY at Rs19mn, with PAT margins improving
to 18% in FY25, compared to -124% in FY22. Management expects organic growth to continue
as more lending and non-lending use cases scale and as regulatory updates, such as expanding
eligible data types and permitting joint accounts, broaden the opportunity. Sahamati is expected
to receive SRO status in 2026, which may formalize industry governance, data-sharing standards
and fair-use norms. Overall ecosystem expansion, recurring data usage, and rising penetration in
MSME and unsecured segments are expected to support continued growth.

In Dec 2025, Finvu raised USD15mn in a Series A round led by WestBridge Capital, bringing
total capital raised to USD17.5mn and implying a post-money valuation of Rs340mn ($3.8mn).
Shareholding post-Series A includes founders at 30-35%, WestBridge Capital at 20-25%, and
strategic investors such as M2P Fintech at 15-18%.
